1: # Pathland Rust Workspace
2: 
3: The Rust core of Pathland: the **opcode engine** that emits the declarative
4: view structure as a fixed 16-byte opcode ring buffer into shared linear memory,
5: consumed by host renderers. Runs natively on desktop (C ABI + GTK renderer);
6: WASM/WIT is the browser/remote projection only.
7: 
8: ```
9: crates/
10: ├── pathland-opcode/   # 16-byte opcode, ring buffer, bump arena, linear-memory layout (no_std)
11: ├── pathland-view/     # SwiftUI-style view DSL: VStack/HStack/Text/Button + decoupled
12: │                      #   chainable modifiers (spacing/padding/fontSize/color/background) (no_std)
13: ├── pathland-engine/   # retained view tree -> declarative TREE/STYLE opcodes,
14: │                      #   diff-based reactive emission (zero-alloc steady state)
15: ├── pathland-host/     # host reader: ring -> native-element description (std layer)
16: ├── pathland-transport/# opcode transport: shared-memory ring + network batch encode/decode
17: │                      #   + batching policy + transport abstraction (RingTransport/FrameSource)
18: ├── pathland-guest/    # WASM guest component: retained tree + engine + emit/take-batch (browser)
19: ├── pathland-wit-host/ # WIT host bindings + DSL bridge (wasmtime embed, remote hosts)
20: ├── pathland-native/   # native C-ABI shim + NativeHost: flat world over a zero-copy shared ring
21: ├── pathland-gtk/      # GTK4 RENDERER (rlib + cdylib): opcode frames -> native GTK widgets
22: │                      #   (incremental); the only crate that touches GTK/glib/pango
23: ├── pathland-codegen/  # DSL code generator: parses lib/ui/components.yaml, asserts ids,
24: │                      #   emits the checked-in Java DSL
25: └── pathland-gtk-demo/ # GTK4 desktop demo: authors the DSL, renders through pathland-gtk
26:                        #   (uses NO GTK APIs directly)
27: 
28: # Cross-language demo
29: ../java/pathland-demo/ # Java (Maven): SwiftUI-like DSL + JNA over pathland-native,
30:                        #   rendered through pathland-gtk (uses NO Swing / NO GTK APIs)
31: ```
32: 
33: ## Specification
34: 
35: - [`spec/OPCODE.md`](../../spec/OPCODE.md) — the 16-byte opcode protocol
36: - [`spec/CONFORMANCE.md`](../../spec/CONFORMANCE.md) — golden byte vectors
37: - [`wit/pathland.wit`](../../wit/pathland.wit) — the WIT component world
38: 
39: ## Run tests
40: 
41: ```bash
42: PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo test
43: ```
44: 
45: ## Run the GTK desktop demo (native, zero-copy shared ring)
46: 
47: ```bash
48: PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo run -p pathland-gtk-demo
49: ```
50: 
51: Requires GTK4 (`brew install gtk4` on macOS).
52: 
53: ## Run the Java demo (cross-language, JNA over the native C-ABI shim + GTK renderer)
54: 
55: ```bash
56: PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo build -p pathland-native -p pathland-gtk
57: cd ../java/pathland-demo && mvn -q -Dpathland.rust.target=<lib/rust/target/debug> compile exec:java
58: ```
59: 
60: On macOS, GTK must run on the main thread: prefix the mvn command with
61: `MAVEN_OPTS="-XstartOnFirstThread"`.
62: 
63: The Java app uses a SwiftUI-like DSL, drives the Rust engine via the flat
64: `pathland_native_*` C ABI (no per-component wrappers), and renders through the
65: shared `pathland-gtk` renderer (in-process via JNA). It uses **no Swing and no
66: GTK APIs directly** — native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes through the
67: shared ring, and the host drains them via `pathland_native_drain_events`. Verify
68: headlessly with `-Dexec.mainClass=demo.DemoHeadless`.
69: 
70: 
71: ## Build for wasm32 (browser projection only)
72: 
73: ```bash
74: RUSTC=~/.rustup/toolchains/stable-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin/rustc \
75:   cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
76: ```
77: 
78: > The Homebrew `cargo` on PATH resolves a rustc without the wasm std. Use the
79: > rustup toolchain's rustc via `RUSTC=...` (or `rustup run stable cargo`).
80: 
81: ## Engine example
82: 
83: The engine emits declarative structure (no rects). A signal changes a property;
84: the next `emit` writes only the delta opcodes.
85: 
86: ```rust
87: use pathland_engine::Engine;
88: use pathland_opcode::{init_memory, Guest, MemoryLayout};
89: use pathland_view::{assign_ids, text, vstack, View, ViewExt};
90: 
91: let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
92: let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
93: init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
94: 
95: let mut guest = Guest::new(&mut mem, &layout);
96: let mut engine = Engine::new();
97: 
98: let mut root = vstack![text("Hello")]
99:     .spacing(4.0)
100:     .padding(8.0)
101:     .build();
102: assign_ids(&mut root, &mut 1);
103: 
104: guest.begin_frame();
105: engine.emit(&root, &mut guest).unwrap(); // full structure
106: guest.end_frame();
107: 
108: root.properties.insert(pathland_opcode::property_id::SPACING, 12.0f32.to_bits());
109: 
110: guest.begin_frame();
111: engine.emit(&root, &mut guest).unwrap(); // exactly one SET_PROPERTY
112: guest.end_frame();
113: ```
114: 
115: Emission in the steady state allocates nothing; only changed nodes produce
116: opcodes, so an unchanged tree emits zero opcodes. Native renderers map the
117: structure onto their native elements (GTK4 widgets, DOM elements).
118: 
119: ## Network transport example
120: 
121: Frames emitted into the ring can be serialized into network batches and flushed
122: on a time/size policy (`BatchEncoder` / `Batcher`); a `BatchDecoder` rebuilds a
123: `Frame`-compatible view so the same `RenderTree::apply_frame` consumes batches
124: and shared-memory frames identically. See `spec/OPCODE.md#transport`.

(End of file - total 124 lines)

1: # Pathland Protocol
2: 
3: > A cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol inspired by SwiftUI
4: 
5: ## Overview
6: 
7: Pathland is a **protocol-first** UI framework for **retained-mode UI** with
8: multiple renderer backends. It's inspired by SwiftUI's declarative syntax, but
9: designed to be **language-agnostic** and **platform-agnostic**.
10: 
11: As of August 2026 the core is a **Rust opcode engine**. It emits the
12: application's **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing,
13: padding, alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring buffer** into shared
14: linear memory. Each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that
15: platform's **native elements** (GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the
16: browser, HTML server-side) and those native elements lay themselves out.
17: 
18: On desktop the engine runs **natively**: other languages drive it through the
19: flat **native C ABI** (`pathland-native`) over a zero-copy shared ring and render
20: through the shared GTK renderer (`pathland-gtk`). **WASM/WIT are the
21: browser/remote projection only**, not the primary path.
22: 
23: **The engine does not compute layout and does not emit rects.** It describes
24: *what* the UI is, never *where* it is. Emission is **diff-based and reactive**:
25: signals in the application ensure only changed nodes emit opcodes, so an
26: unchanged tree emits zero opcodes.
27: 
28: ## The Three Elements
29: 
30: Pathland is composed of three elements. They are the vocabulary the whole
31: project speaks, so they are settled and used consistently:
32: 
33: ```
34: ┌────────────────────┐        ┌─────────────────────┐
35: │ 1. Retained UI     │        │ 3. Renderer         │
36: │ the app's UI tree  │────┐   │ maps opcodes onto   │
37: │ (any language,     │    │   │ native elements +   │
38: │  any platform)     │    │   │ event reporting     │
39: └────────────────────┘    │   └───────────▲─────────┘
40:                          │                │
41: ┌────────────────────┐    │                │
42: │ 2. Opcode engine   │◄───┘                │
43: │ diffs + emits      │─────────────────────┘
44: └────────────────────┘
45: ```
46: 
47: 1. **Retained UI** — the application's canonical retained UI tree. It is the
48:    single source of truth, owned by the application. It can be authored in
49:    **any language on any platform**: Rust, Java, Swift, C#, C, TypeScript —
50:    desktop, mobile, embedded, or web — through a generated DSL, a WIT binding,
51:    or the flat native C ABI.
52: 2. **Opcode engine** — walks the retained tree, diffs it, and emits fixed
53:    **16-byte opcodes** (the producer). Emission is reactive: only changed nodes
54:    emit, so an unchanged tree emits zero opcodes. The engine is
55:    language-independent — the same opcode stream serves every renderer.
56: 3. **Renderer** — consumes the opcode stream and maps it onto that platform's
57:    **native elements**, and reports raw inputs back as events. It is a pure
58:    function of the opcode stream (stateless) and never retains application
59:    state. *"Host" and "driver" are roles a renderer plays: it runs inside a
60:    host and is pumped by a driver — they are not separate elements.* The same
61:    opcode stream targets **different UI systems**: a GTK4 renderer on desktop,
62:    an AppKit/SwiftUI renderer on macOS, a WinUI renderer on Windows, an LVGL
63:    renderer on embedded, a DOM renderer in the browser.
64: 
65: The opcodes are carried from the engine to the renderer by a transport (a
66: zero-copy shared-memory ring on desktop/native, a serialized network batch for
67: remote/browser); transport is an implementation detail, not a fourth element.
68: 
69: ## Core Principles
70: 
71: - **Protocol-first**: standardized, open protocol for UI components, events, and raw inputs
72: - **16-byte opcodes**: every instruction is a fixed 16 bytes — cache-line aligned, deterministic, linear decode
73: - **Declarative, not positioned**: the engine emits structure + constraint properties (spacing, padding, alignment); native renderers compute positions
74: - **Native elements everywhere**: GTK4 widgets, DOM elements, HTML — never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent
75: - **Reactive emission**: only the nodes that changed emit opcodes; steady state emits zero
76: - **Command-based**: UI updates are tree mutations (CREATE_NODE, DELETE_NODE, INSERT_CHILD, MOVE_CHILD, …), never serialized trees
77: - **Stateless renderers**: renderers are pure functions of the opcode stream; they retain only their own rendered output, never application state
78: - **Zero-copy**: ring and arena are plain regions of shared linear memory
79: - **Single-producer / single-consumer**: guest engine produces; host renderer consumes
80: - **Catalog-driven DSL**: the ergonomic SwiftUI-like DSL in any language is generated from a single YAML catalog (`lib/ui/`), not hand-written
81: 
82: ## Documentation
83: 
84: ### Specification
85: 
86: - [Opcode Protocol](./spec/OPCODE.md) — **Primary specification** — fixed 16-byte opcodes, ring buffer, arena, reactive emission, design tokens
87: - [Conformance Test Vectors](./spec/CONFORMANCE.md) — golden byte arrays for validating implementations
88: 
89: ## Rust Workspace
90: 
91: The implementation is under [`lib/rust/`](./lib/rust/):
92: 
93: | Crate | Responsibility |
94: |-------|----------------|
95: | `pathland-opcode` | 16-byte opcode, ring buffer, bump arena, linear-memory layout (`no_std`) |
96: | `pathland-view` | SwiftUI-style view DSL: VStack/HStack/Text/Button + chainable modifiers (`no_std`) |
97: | `pathland-engine` | Retained view tree → declarative `TREE`/`STYLE` opcodes; diff-based reactive emission (zero-alloc steady state) |
98: | `pathland-host` | Host reader: ring → native-element description (`std` convenience layer) |
99: | `pathland-transport` | Opcode transport: shared-memory ring + network batch encode/decode + transport abstraction |
100: | `pathland-native` | Native C-ABI shim + `NativeHost`: flat world over a zero-copy shared ring (Swift/Java/C#…) |
101: | `pathland-gtk` | GTK4 renderer (rlib + cdylib): opcode frames → native GTK widgets, incrementally |
102: | `pathland-gtk-demo` | Rust GTK4 demo: authors the DSL, renders through `pathland-gtk` (no GTK APIs) |
103: | `pathland-codegen` | DSL code generator: parses `lib/ui/components.yaml`, asserts ids, emits the Java DSL |
104: | `pathland-guest` | WASM guest component (browser/remote only) |
105: | `pathland-wit-host` | WIT host bindings + DSL bridge (browser/remote only) |
106: 
107: The DSL catalog lives in [`lib/ui/components.yaml`](./lib/ui/components.yaml);
108: regenerate the Java DSL with `./generate.sh`.
109: 
110: ### Run tests
111: 
112: ```bash
113: cd lib/rust
114: cargo test
115: ```
116: 
117: ### Run the demos (native, zero-copy shared ring + GTK renderer)
118: 
119: ```bash
120: # Rust demo
121: cd lib/rust && PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo run -p pathland-gtk-demo
122: 
123: # Java demo (JNA over pathland-native + pathland-gtk)
124: PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo build -p pathland-native -p pathland-gtk
125: cd lib/java/pathland-demo && mvn -q -Dpathland.rust.target=<lib/rust/target/debug> compile exec:java
126: ```
127: 
128: On macOS the Java demo must run GTK on the main thread:
129: `MAVEN_OPTS="-XstartOnFirstThread"`.
130: 
131: ### Build for wasm32 (browser projection only)
132: 
133: ```bash
134: RUSTC=~/.rustup/toolchains/stable-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin/rustc \
135:   cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
136: ```
137: 
138: ## Components & Properties
139: 
140: Component and property IDs are defined in `pathland-opcode`'s
141: [`constants.rs`](./lib/rust/crates/pathland-opcode/src/constants.rs) and
142: documented in [OPCODE.md](./spec/OPCODE.md). Component types include `HSTACK`,
143: `VSTACK`, `TEXT`, `BUTTON`, `SPACER`, and more; stack constraint properties
144: (`SPACING`, `ALIGNMENT`, …) drive native layout, styling modifiers (`PADDING`,
145: `COLOR`, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, …) decorate any view, and `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`
146: use `-1` = FILL, `-2` = HUG_CONTENT.
147: 
148: ## Design Tokens
149: 
150: The renderer owns default token values; the application owns overrides.
151: Tokens are identified by dot-separated paths (`color.primary`, `space.2`) and
152: referenced via the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type or overridden globally with
153: `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`. See [Design Token System](./spec/OPCODE.md#design-token-system).
154: 
155: ## Roadmap (POC Goals)
156: 
157: See the GitHub issues (#12, #13, #15, #16, #18):
158: 
159: 1. **16-byte opcode engine** — done
160: 2. **Core components & modifiers in Rust** (SwiftUI-like API) — done
161: 3. **Opcode transport layer** (shared memory + network batch + native C-ABI shim) — done
162: 4. **Rust desktop app with GTK4 renderer** (native shared ring) — done
163: 5. **Catalog-driven DSL** (YAML → Java via `pathland-codegen`) — done
164: 6. Quarkus SSR + WebSocket demo — planned
165: 
166: ## Versioning
167: 
168: Pathland follows **Semantic Versioning** (Major.Minor.Patch). The wire protocol
169: version is 1 (see [OPCODE.md](./spec/OPCODE.md)).
170: 
171: ## License
172: 
173: Pathland is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for details.

(End of file - total 173 lines)
</content>

1: //! # pathland-host
2: //!
3: //! Host-side reader for the Pathland 16-byte opcode ring. Consumes frames from
4: //! shared linear memory and builds a **native-element description**: the tree
5: //! structure (`TREE`) plus constraint properties (`STYLE`) a renderer maps onto
6: //! that platform's native elements (GTK widgets, DOM elements, HTML).
7: //!
8: //! The engine does not compute layout; this crate stores only what the renderer
9: //! needs to create native elements and let them lay themselves out.
10: 
11: use std::collections::HashMap;
12: 
13: pub use pathland_engine;
14: pub use pathland_opcode;
15: 
16: use pathland_opcode::category;
17: use pathland_opcode::component_type;
18: use pathland_opcode::style;
19: use pathland_opcode::tree;
20: use pathland_opcode::{Frame, Opcode};
21: 
22: /// A decoded node in the host's native-element description.
23: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
24: pub struct HostNode {
25:     pub id: u32,
26:     pub component_type: u16,
27:     pub text: Option<String>,
28:     pub parent: Option<u32>,
29:     pub children: Vec<u32>,
30:     /// Constraint properties (propertyId → value) for native layout/styling.
31:     pub properties: HashMap<u16, u32>,
32: }
33: 
34: impl Default for HostNode {
35:     fn default() -> Self {
36:         Self {
37:             id: 0,
38:             component_type: component_type::HSTACK,
39:             text: None,
40:             parent: None,
41:             children: Vec::new(),
42:             properties: HashMap::new(),
43:         }
44:     }
45: }
46: 
47: /// The host's native-element description of a rendered tree.
48: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
49: pub struct RenderTree {
50:     /// nodeId → node.
51:     pub nodes: HashMap<u32, HostNode>,
52: }
53: 
54: impl RenderTree {
55:     /// Apply a frame's opcodes to this tree (a delta).
56:     pub fn apply_frame(&mut self, frame: &Frame<'_>) {
57:         for op in frame.opcodes() {
58:             match (op.category(), op.command()) {
59:                 (category::TREE, tree::CREATE_NODE) => {
60:                     let id = op.a();
61:                     let ty = op.b() as u16;
62:                     let entry = self.nodes.entry(id).or_default();
63:                     entry.id = id;
64:                     entry.component_type = ty;
65:                 }
66:                 (category::TREE, tree::DELETE_NODE) => {
67:                     self.nodes.remove(&op.a());
68:                 }
69:                 (category::TREE, tree::INSERT_CHILD) => {
70:                     let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
71:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
72:                         if !p.children.contains(&child) {
73:                             p.children.push(child);
74:                         }
75:                     }
76:                     if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
77:                         c.parent = Some(parent);
78:                     }
79:                 }
80:                 (category::TREE, tree::REMOVE_CHILD) => {
81:                     let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
82:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
83:                         p.children.retain(|c| *c != child);
84:                     }
85:                     if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
86:                         c.parent = None;
87:                     }
88:                 }
89:                 (category::TREE, tree::MOVE_CHILD) => {
90:                     let (parent, child, new_index) = (op.a(), op.b(), op.c() as usize);
91:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
92:                         if let Some(pos) = p.children.iter().position(|c| *c == child) {
93:                             p.children.remove(pos);
94:                         }
95:                         let idx = if new_index == usize::MAX {
96:                             p.children.len()
97:                         } else {
98:                             new_index.min(p.children.len())
99:                         };
100:                         p.children.insert(idx, child);
101:                     }
102:                 }
103:                 (category::STYLE, style::SET_PROPERTY) => {
104:                     let prop_id = op.b() as u16;
105:                     if let Some(n) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
106:                         n.properties.insert(prop_id, op.c());
107:                     }
108:                 }
109:                 (category::STYLE, style::SET_TEXT) => {
110:                     if let Some(n) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
111:                         n.text = frame.arena_str(op.b()).ok().map(|s| s.to_string());
112:                     }
113:                 }
114:                 (category::STYLE, style::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN) => {
115:                     // Token overrides are handled by the renderer's theme layer.
116:                     let _ = op;
117:                 }
118:                 _ => {}
119:             }
120:         }
121:     }
122: 
123:     /// Look up a node by id.
124:     pub fn node(&self, id: u32) -> Option<&HostNode> {
125:         self.nodes.get(&id)
126:     }
127: 
128:     /// The root node: the single node without a parent.
129:     pub fn root(&self) -> Option<&HostNode> {
130:         self.nodes.values().find(|n| n.parent.is_none())
131:     }
132: }
133: 
134: /// Decode a frame into a fresh `RenderTree`.
135: pub fn render_tree_from_frame(frame: &Frame<'_>) -> RenderTree {
136:     let mut tree = RenderTree::default();
137:     tree.apply_frame(frame);
138:     tree
139: }
140: 
141: /// Convert a single opcode into a human-readable line (debugging aid).
142: pub fn describe(op: &Opcode) -> String {
143:     match (op.category(), op.command()) {
144:         (category::TREE, tree::CREATE_NODE) => {
145:             format!("TREE:CREATE_NODE id={} type=0x{:04x}", op.a(), op.b() as u16)
146:         }
147:         (category::TREE, tree::DELETE_NODE) => format!("TREE:DELETE_NODE id={}", op.a()),
148:         (category::TREE, tree::INSERT_CHILD) => format!(
149:             "TREE:INSERT_CHILD parent={} child={} index={}",
150:             op.a(),
151:             op.b(),
152:             op.c()
153:         ),
154:         (category::TREE, tree::REMOVE_CHILD) => {
155:             format!("TREE:REMOVE_CHILD parent={} child={}", op.a(), op.b())
156:         }
157:         (category::TREE, tree::MOVE_CHILD) => format!(
158:             "TREE:MOVE_CHILD parent={} child={} index={}",
159:             op.a(),
160:             op.b(),
161:             op.c()
162:         ),
163:         (category::STYLE, style::SET_PROPERTY) => format!(
164:             "STYLE:SET_PROPERTY id={} prop=0x{:04x} value=0x{:08x}",
165:             op.a(),
166:             op.b() as u16,
167:             op.c()
168:         ),
169:         (category::STYLE, style::SET_TEXT) => {
170:             format!("STYLE:SET_TEXT id={} arenaRef={}", op.a(), op.b())
171:         }
172:         _ => format!("{:?}", op),
173:     }
174: }
175: 
176: #[cfg(test)]
177: mod tests {
178:     use super::*;
179:     use pathland_engine::Engine;
180:     use pathland_opcode::{init_memory, Guest, MemoryLayout};

215:         let child = tree.node(2).unwrap();

1: //! # pathland-transport
2: //!
3: //! How Pathland opcodes are transported from the guest engine to host
4: //! renderers. There are two peer backends:
5: //!
6: //! - **Shared memory** (desktop/native): the ring buffer + arena in
7: //!   `pathland-opcode` (`Guest`/`Host`). Zero-copy. This crate treats it as
8: //!   the local transport — no duplication.
9: //! - **Network batch** (SSR → browser): opcodes + arena data serialized into
10: //!   **batches**, flushed on a **time interval** or a **network-frame size**
11: //!   (whichever comes first).
12: //!
13: //! `pathland_opcode::Frame` is the **transport seam**: `pathland-host`'s
14: //! `RenderTree::apply_frame` consumes frames regardless of origin. `BatchDecoder`
15: //! produces `Frame` views over decoded batches, so a network batch feeds the
16: //! renderer exactly like a shared-memory frame.
17: //!
18: //! ## Batch wire format
19: //!
20: //! ```text
21: //! magic "PLPL" (u32 LE) | version (u16) | flags (u16) | frameCount (u32)
22: //! | opcodeCount (u32) | opcodes (16 B × opcodeCount) | arenaDeltaLen (u32)
23: //! | arena delta bytes
24: //! ```
25: //!
26: //! The arena is append-only (bump); batches carry only the bytes appended since
27: //! the previous batch. The decoder appends them to a mirrored arena, so absolute
28: //! `arenaRef` offsets stay valid — exactly as in shared memory.
29: //!
30: //! ## Example (producer)
31: //!
32: //! ```no_run
33: //! use pathland_transport::{Batcher, BatchPolicy, BatchEncoder};
34: //! use std::time::Duration;
35: //!
36: //! let policy = BatchPolicy::new(Duration::from_millis(4), 1400);
37: //! let mut batcher = Batcher::new(policy);
38: //! let mut encoder = BatchEncoder::new();
39: //!
40: //! // batcher.push_frame(&frame) accumulates opcodes + arena delta;
41: //! // batcher.flush() -> Option<Vec<u8>> produces the serialized batch.
42: //! ```
43: 
44: #![forbid(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]
45: 
46: extern crate alloc;
47: 
48: mod batch;
49: mod batching;
50: mod conformance;
51: mod net;
52: mod ring;
53: mod traits;
54: 
55: pub use batch::{encode_batch, Batch, BatchDecoder, BatchEncoder};
56: pub use batching::{Batcher, BatchPolicy};
57: pub use net::NetBatchEncoder;
58: pub use ring::RingTransport;
59: pub use traits::{
60:     DriverTransport, FrameSource, InputSink, OpcodeBatch, ProtocolError, TransportError,
61: };
62: 
63: /// Wire magic for network batches (`PLPL`).
64: pub const BATCH_MAGIC: u32 = 0x504C_504C;
65: /// Wire version for the batch format.
66: pub const BATCH_VERSION: u16 = 1;
67: 
68: /// Direction of a batch. Events are not yet implemented; this bit is reserved.
69: pub mod direction {
70:     /// The batch carries guest → host tree/style opcodes.
71:     pub const GUEST_TO_HOST: u16 = 0x0000;
72:     /// The batch carries host → guest raw-input events (reserved).
73:     pub const HOST_TO_GUEST: u16 = 0x0001;
74: }

1: //! # pathland-native
2: //!
3: //! Native (non-WASM) projection of the Pathland flat world, exposed over both a
4: //! Rust API and a C ABI for foreign host languages (Swift / Java / C# / …).
5: //!
6: //! This is the **cross-language, zero-copy** path: a host links this crate as a
7: //! native library (or a `cdylib` and its `pathland_native_*` C functions), drives
8: //! the retained tree with the flat `builder`/`engine` operations, and reads
9: //! opcodes from the **shared-memory ring in place** — no serialization, no batch,
10: //! no WASM.
11: //!
12: //! The surface mirrors `wit/pathland.wit` (`builder`, `engine`) but for a native
13: //! shared-memory transport instead of a WASM/WIT ABI.
14: 
15: use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap};
16: 
17: use pathland_engine::Engine;
18: use pathland_opcode::{component_type, property_id, MemoryLayout};
19: use pathland_transport::{
20:     DriverTransport, FrameSource, OpcodeBatch, RingTransport, TransportError,
21: };
22: use pathland_view::{component_type_id, Node};
23: 
24: mod capi;
25: 
26: /// A flat node in the host's retained tree (id → node).
27: #[derive(Clone)]
28: pub struct FlatNode {
29:     pub id: u32,
30:     pub view_component: pathland_view::Component,
31:     pub properties: BTreeMap<u16, u32>,
32:     pub parent: Option<u32>,
33:     pub children: Vec<u32>,
34: }
35: 
36: /// The native host: owns the retained tree, the diff engine, and the shared
37: /// zero-copy ring.
38: pub struct NativeHost {
39:     nodes: HashMap<u32, FlatNode>,
40:     engine: Engine,
41:     ring: RingTransport,
42: }
43: 
44: /// Safe, checked operations returning `()` (used by the C shim).
45: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
46: pub enum HostError {
47:     /// The operation referenced a missing node.
48:     NotFound,
49: }
50: 
51: impl NativeHost {
52:     /// Create a host with a fresh shared ring (default layout).
53:     pub fn new() -> Self {
54:         Self {
55:             nodes: HashMap::new(),
56:             engine: Engine::new(),
57:             ring: RingTransport::new(),
58:         }
59:     }
60: 
61:     /// Create a host over a caller-provided ring buffer + layout.
62:     pub fn with_buffer(mem: Vec<u8>, layout: MemoryLayout) -> Self {
63:         Self {
64:             nodes: HashMap::new(),
65:             engine: Engine::new(),
66:             ring: RingTransport::with_buffer(mem, layout),
67:         }
68:     }
69: 
70:     /// Create (or reset) a node with a host-supplied stable id.
71:     pub fn create_node(&mut self, id: u32, component: pathland_view::Component) {
72:         let entry = self.nodes.entry(id).or_insert(FlatNode {
73:             id,
74:             view_component: component.clone(),
75:             properties: BTreeMap::new(),
76:             parent: None,
77:             children: Vec::new(),
78:         });
79:         entry.view_component = component;
80:         entry.properties.clear();
81:     }
82: 
83:     /// Insert `child` into `parent` at `index` (u32::MAX appends).
84:     pub fn insert_child(&mut self, parent: u32, child: u32, index: u32) {
85:         if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
86:             let idx = if index == u32::MAX {
87:                 p.children.len()
88:             } else {
89:                 (index as usize).min(p.children.len())
90:             };
91:             if !p.children.contains(&child) {
92:                 p.children.insert(idx, child);
93:             }

96:             c.parent = Some(parent);

102:         if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
103:             p.children.retain(|c| *c != child);

134:     /// Emit the retained tree as opcodes into the shared ring.
135:     ///
136:     /// Returns `true` if a frame was written (i.e. the tree is non-empty).
137:     pub fn emit(&mut self) -> bool {
138:         let root = self.root_id().and_then(|r| self.materialize(r));
139:         if let Some(root) = root {
140:             let mut guest = self.ring.producer();
141:             guest.begin_frame();
142:             let _ = self.engine.emit(&root, &mut guest);
143:             guest.end_frame();
144:             true

146:             false
147:         }

174:     /// Materialize a `pathland_view::Node` subtree rooted at `id`.
175:     fn materialize(&self, id: u32) -> Option<Node> {
176:         let flat = self.nodes.get(&id)?.clone();
177:         let mut node = Node::from_component(&flat.view_component);
178:         node.id = flat.id;

1: //! # pathland-engine
2: //!
3: //! The Pathland **guest engine**. It holds the application's **retained view
4: //! tree** (built with the SwiftUI-style DSL in `pathland-view`) and emits the
5: //! **declarative structure** as `TREE`/`STYLE` opcodes into the 16-byte ring
6: //! buffer — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding, alignment. It does **not**
7: //! compute rects or layout; native renderers (GTK4 widgets, DOM flexbox) lay
8: //! out their own native elements from these constraints.
9: //!
10: //! ## Reactive emission
11: //!
12: //! Emission is **diff-based**: on each `emit` the engine compares the current
13: //! tree against a snapshot of what it last emitted, and writes only the
14: //! opcodes for nodes that actually changed. An unchanged tree emits **zero**
15: //! opcodes. This is what signals in the application drive — a signal marks the
16: //! tree dirty; `emit` reconciles.
17: //!
18: //! Both **property diffs** (`SET_PROPERTY`, `SET_TEXT`) and **structural diffs**
19: //! (`CREATE_NODE`, `DELETE_NODE`, `INSERT_CHILD`, `REMOVE_CHILD`, `MOVE_CHILD`)
20: //! are emitted.
21: //!
22: //! ## Zero allocation
23: //!
24: //! The emit pass performs **zero dynamic heap allocations** in the steady
25: //! state. The snapshot is a preallocated slab indexed by node id; per-pass
26: //! bookkeeping uses generation stamps instead of rebuilding maps. Allocations
27: //! only occur when the tree *grows* (new nodes resize the slab) or a node's
28: //! property set actually changes.
29:

31: #![forbid(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]

61: struct SnapshotNode {
62:     component_type: u16,
63:     parent: Option<u32>,
64:     index: usize,
65:     text: Option<String>,
66:     properties: BTreeMap<u16, u32>,

82: /// The diff-based reactive emitter.
83: ///
84: /// `Engine` keeps the snapshot of what was last emitted. Calling `emit` with a
85: /// (possibly mutated) retained tree writes only the delta opcodes. The steady
86: /// state of the emit pass allocates nothing.
87: pub struct Engine {
88:     /// nodeId → last emitted state (a preallocated slab; node ids are dense).
89:     snapshot: Vec<Option<SnapshotNode>>,
90:     /// Monotonic generation stamp for the current pass.
91:     gen: u64,
92: }
93: 
94: impl Default for Engine {
95:     fn default() -> Self {
96:         Self::new()
97:     }
98: }
99: 
100: impl Engine {
101:     pub fn new() -> Self {
102:         Self {
103:             snapshot: Vec::new(),
104:             gen: 0,
105:         }
106:     }
107: 
108:     /// Reconcile `root` against the snapshot, emitting only changed opcodes.
109:     pub fn emit(
110:         &mut self,
111:         root: &Node,
112:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
113:     ) -> Result<EmitResult, pathland_opcode::RingError> {
114:         self.gen = self.gen.wrapping_add(1);
115:         let mut out = 0usize;
116:         self.reconcile_node(root, None, 0, guest, &mut out)?;
117: 
118:         // Delete any node that existed in the snapshot but was not visited this
119:         // pass (generation stamp unchanged).
120:         for (id, slot) in self.snapshot.iter_mut().enumerate() {
121:             if let Some(s) = slot {
122:                 if s.gen != self.gen {
123:                     guest.delete_node(id as u32)?;
124:                     out += 1;
125:                     *slot = None;
126:                 }
127:             }
128:         }
129:         Ok(EmitResult { opcodes: out })
130:     }
131: 
132:     /// Number of nodes tracked in the snapshot (diagnostics).
133:     pub fn tracked_nodes(&self) -> usize {
134:         self.snapshot.iter().filter(|s| s.is_some()).count()
135:     }
136: 
137:     fn slot_mut(&mut self, id: u32) -> &mut Option<SnapshotNode> {
138:         let idx = id as usize;
139:         if self.snapshot.len() <= idx {
140:             self.snapshot.resize(idx + 1, None);
141:         }
142:         &mut self.snapshot[idx]
143:     }
144: 
145:     #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
146:     fn reconcile_node(
147:         &mut self,
148:         node: &Node,
149:         parent: Option<u32>,
150:         index: usize,
151:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
152:         out: &mut usize,
153:     ) -> Result<(), pathland_opcode::RingError> {
154:         let component_type = component_type_id(&node.component);
155: 
156:         let text_borrowed = match &node.component {
157:             Component::Text { text } => Some(text.as_str()),
158:             Component::Button { label } => Some(label.as_str()),
159:             _ => None,
160:         };
161: 
162:         let prev = self.slot_mut(node.id).take();
163:         let props_changed = match &prev {
164:             Some(p) => p.properties != node.properties,
165:             None => !node.properties.is_empty(),
166:         };
167:         // Text is owned in the snapshot; compare without cloning.
168:         let text_changed = match &prev {
169:             Some(p) => p.text.as_deref() != text_borrowed,
170:             None => text_borrowed.is_some(),
171:         };
172: 
173:         match &prev {
174:             // New node: CREATE_NODE + INSERT_CHILD + all properties/text.
175:             None => {
176:                 guest.create_node(node.id, component_type)?;
177:                 *out += 1;
178:                 if let Some(p) = parent {
179:                     guest.insert_child(p, node.id, index as u32)?;
180:                     *out += 1;
181:                 }
182:                 for (prop, value) in &node.properties {
183:                     guest.set_property(node.id, *prop, value_type_for(*prop), *value)?;
184:                     *out += 1;
185:                 }
186:                 if let Some(t) = text_borrowed {
187:                     guest.set_text(node.id, t)?;
188:                     *out += 1;
189:                 }
190:             }
191:             Some(p) => {
192:                 // Structural changes.
193:                 if p.parent != parent {
194:                     if let Some(old) = p.parent {
195:                         guest.remove_child(old, node.id)?;
196:                         *out += 1;
197:                     }
198:                     if let Some(new) = parent {
199:                         guest.insert_child(new, node.id, index as u32)?;
200:                         *out += 1;
201:                     }
202:                 } else if p.index != index {
203:                     if let Some(par) = parent {
204:                         guest.move_child(par, node.id, index as u32)?;
205:                         *out += 1;
206:                     }
207:                 }
208:                 // Component type changed → recreate.
209:                 if p.component_type != component_type {
210:                     guest.create_node(node.id, component_type)?;
211:                     *out += 1;
212:                 }
213:                 // Text diff.
214:                 if text_changed {
215:                     if let Some(t) = text_borrowed {
216:                         guest.set_text(node.id, t)?;
217:                         *out += 1;
218:                     }
219:                 }
220:                 // Generic property diffs (new or changed values only). This
221:                 // covers stack spacing, styling modifiers (padding, fonts,
222:                 // colors), the `frame` sizing modifier (WIDTH/HEIGHT/ALIGNMENT),
223:                 // and any other modifier applied to the node.
224:                 for (prop, value) in &node.properties {
225:                     if p.properties.get(prop) != Some(value) {
226:                         guest.set_property(node.id, *prop, value_type_for(*prop), *value)?;
227:                         *out += 1;
228:                     }
229:                 }
230:             }
231:         }
232: 
233:         // Store the current state for the next pass. When the property map and
234:         // text are unchanged, move the previous allocations back so the steady
235:         // state allocates nothing; otherwise build fresh values.
236:         let mut prev_props = None;
237:         let mut prev_text = None;
238:         if let Some(p) = prev {
239:             if !props_changed {
240:                 prev_props = Some(p.properties);
241:             }
242:             if !text_changed {
243:                 prev_text = p.text;
244:             }
245:             // If both moved out, `p` is fully consumed.
246:             let _ = p;
247:         }
248:         let properties = match prev_props {
249:             Some(props) => props,
250:             None => node.properties.clone(),
251:         };
252:         let text = match prev_text {
253:             Some(t) => Some(t),
254:             None => text_borrowed.map(|s| s.to_owned()),
255:         };
256:         *self.slot_mut(node.id) = Some(SnapshotNode {
257:             component_type,
258:             parent,
259:             index,
260:             text,
261:             properties,
262:             gen: self.gen,
263:         });
264: 
265:         for (i, child) in node.children.iter().enumerate() {
266:             self.reconcile_node(child, Some(node.id), i, guest, out)?;
267:         }
268:         Ok(())
269:     }
270: }

2: //!
3: //! The producer (opcode engine) and consumer (native driver) share one linear
4: //! memory buffer containing the ring + arena. The producer writes 16-byte
5: //! opcodes via `pathland_opcode::Guest`; the consumer reads completed frames via
6: //! `pathland_opcode::Host`. No copying, no batching, no serialization — this is

13: /// A zero-copy SPSC shared-memory ring transport.
14: ///
15: /// Owns the linear-memory buffer (header + ring + arena). Producers and
16: /// consumers are granted short-lived `Guest`/`Host` views over the same buffer
17: /// via the borrowed methods, so opcodes flow in place with no copies.
18: #[derive(Debug)]
19: pub struct RingTransport {
20:     /// Shared linear memory (header | ring | arena).
21:     mem: Vec<u8>,
22:     /// Ring/arena geometry.
23:     layout: MemoryLayout,
24: }

26: impl RingTransport {
27:     /// Create a ring transport with a default layout and a zeroed header.
28:     pub fn new() -> Self {
29:         let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
30:         let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
31:         init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
32:         Self { mem, layout }
33:     }
34:

36:     pub fn with_buffer(mem: Vec<u8>, layout: MemoryLayout) -> Self {
37:         Self { mem, layout }

42:         &self.layout

46:     ///
47:     /// Drop the returned `Guest` before calling `next_frame`; producer and
48:     /// consumer must not overlap borrows.
49:     pub fn producer(&mut self) -> Guest<'_> {
50:         Guest::new(&mut self.mem, &self.layout)

## Plan: Simplify the `lib/rust` crate structure

### Diagnosis — why it feels fragmented

The repo says the system has **three elements** (Retained UI, Opcode engine, Renderer), but the crate boundaries and names don't surface them. Mapping the 11 crates today:

| Element | Crates involved |
|---|---|
| 1. Retained UI | `pathland-view` (DSL + `Node` tree) |
| 2. Opcode engine | `pathland-opcode` (format/ring/arena) + `pathland-engine` (diff emit) + `pathland-transport` (carrier) |
| 3. Renderer | `pathland-host` (`RenderTree` decode) + `pathland-gtk` (native mapping) |
| Not an element (projection / demo / tool) | `pathland-guest`, `pathland-wit-host`, `pathland-native`, `pathland-gtk-demo`, `pathland-codegen` |

Two problems stand out:
1. **Element 2 is split across 3 crates**, and two crates both self-describe as "the engine" (`pathland-opcode`'s lib.rs literally says "the 16-byte opcode engine"; `pathland-engine` is the diff emitter).
2. **Thin layers exist only to be wired together**: `pathland-host` is 270 lines and its *only* production consumer is `pathland-gtk`; `pathland-transport`'s `ring.rs` (255 lines) just re-wraps `pathland-opcode`'s `Guest`/`Host`.

### Hard constraints (verified, not opinions)

These prevent a naive "3 crates = 3 elements" collapse:

- **Dependency cycle**: `opcode ← view ← engine` (`engine` needs `view::Node`; `view` needs `opcode` constants). You *cannot* merge `engine` into `opcode` without also merging `view`, which would erase the Element-1/Element-2 boundary.
- **`no_std` boundary**: `opcode`, `view`, `engine` are `no_std`; `transport` is `std` (uses `std::time::Duration`). Folding `transport` into the `no_std` core forces a `std` feature-gate or dropping `no_std`.
- **Crate-type locks**: `pathland-guest` (wasm32 component, WIT world), `pathland-native` (`cdylib` + `rlib`), `pathland-gtk` (`cdylib` + `rlib`, only place touching GTK) must stay separate.
- **External references to stable names**: `generate.sh` (`cargo run -p pathland-codegen`), `run.sh` (`cargo build -p pathland-native -p pathland-gtk`), and JNA symbols `pathland_native_*` / `pathland_gtk_*` (via `[lib] name`, not crate name — safe to rename crates as long as `[lib] name` stays).

### Recommended target structure (11 → 8 crates)

Three core libraries aligned to the elements, plus projections/demo/tool that are *clearly labeled* as such:

```
crates/
├── pathland-view/        # Element 1 — Retained UI (DSL + Node tree)   [no_std, unchanged]
├── pathland-opcode/      # Element 2 — Opcode engine (opcode format + ring + arena)
│                         #   + diff emitter (absorbs pathland-engine)
├── pathland-transport/   # Element 2 — transport (ring ownership + network batch)  [std, unchanged]
├── pathland-gtk/         # Element 3 — Renderer (absorbs pathland-host's RenderTree)
├── pathland-native/      # Projection — native C-ABI shim + NativeHost   [host/driver role]
├── pathland-guest/       # Projection — WASM component (browser/remote)
├── pathland-wit-host/    # Projection — wasmtime host bridge (browser/remote)
├── pathland-codegen/     # Tool — DSL generator (bin)
└── pathland-gtk-demo/    # Demo — bin
```

Concrete changes:
1. **Merge `pathland-engine` → `pathland-opcode`** (both `no_std`; engine is 583 lines). `view` stays a dependency, so no cycle. Resolves the "two engines" confusion; Element 2 = format + emitter in one crate. *(Alt: keep `pathland-engine` as a submodule `engine.rs` inside `pathland-opcode` for zero-churn.)*
2. **Merge `pathland-host` → `pathland-gtk`** (270 lines, sole production consumer). `RenderTree`/`HostNode` move into `pathland-gtk` as the renderer's decode layer; dev-deps in `native`/`wit-host`/`transport` retarget to `pathland-gtk` (or the `RenderTree` moves to `pathland-opcode` as a `std` reader — see open question below).
3. **Keep `pathland-transport` separate** but re-document it as part of Element 2 (the README already calls transport "an implementation detail, not a fourth element"). Avoids the `no_std` breakage.
4. **Naming/grouping only** (no moves): add a `lib/rust/README.md` section + `Cargo.toml` comments mapping each crate to its element/projection role. Update the root `README.md` crate table to the 3-element grouping.

### Open questions (blocking final shape)

Two tradeoffs I need your call on before I write the execution steps:

questions.question: `pathland-host`'s `RenderTree` (opcode → native-element description) is used only by `pathland-gtk` today. Where should it go after the merge?

options.label: Fold into pathland-gtk (Recommended)
options.description: Simplest: Element 3 becomes a single renderer crate. Re-extract a shared decode crate later if a DOM/HTML renderer appears (YAGNI).

options.label: Fold into pathland-opcode
options.description: Keep RenderTree as a reusable, renderer-agnostic 'std' reader inside the engine crate, so future renderers share it. Requires a std feature-gate in the no_std core.

questions.question: The diff emitter (`pathland-engine`, 583 lines) should become part of Element 2. How aggressive?

options.label: Merge crate into pathland-opcode (Recommended)
options.description: Delete pathland-engine; move its code into pathland-opcode (e.g. as engine.rs). One crate = opcode format + diff emitter. Some import churn.

options.label: Keep as submodule only
options.description: Keep pathland-engine as a crate but re-document it as Element 2 with opcode; only fix naming/README. Lowest churn, but leaves the 'two engines' confusion.

questions.question: Do you want crates renamed to make the element mapping self-evident (e.g. pathland-view, pathland-engine, pathland-render), or keep existing names?

options.label: Keep existing names (Recommended)
options.description: Rename only via docs/comments. Avoids touching Cargo.toml members, scripts, and imports. Lowest risk.

options.label: Rename to element-aligned names
options.description: e.g. pathland-gtk → pathland-render-gtk, pathland-opcode → pathland-engine. Clearer mapping but touches every import + script reference.

## Plan: simplify `lib/rust` to a 3-element structure

### ⚠️ One correction to your "merge engine → opcode" choice

That specific merge is **blocked by a dependency cycle**:

```
pathland-opcode (constants/format)  ←  pathland-view (DSL + Node)  ←  pathland-engine (diff emitter)
```

- `pathland-engine` depends on `pathland_view::Node` (and `component_type_id`, `value_type_for`)
- `pathland-view` depends on `pathland_opcode::*` constants

If the diff emitter moved into `pathland-opcode`, then `opcode` would need `view::Node` while `view` needs `opcode` constants → Cargo rejects the cycle. The **valid equivalent** is to merge the diff emitter into its dependency, `pathland-view` (same net effect: one fewer crate, the emitter stops being its own crate). I'll proceed on that basis unless you object.

### Target structure — 11 → 9 crates, each mapping to an element

```
crates/
├── pathland-view/          # Element 1 — Retained UI: DSL + Node tree + diff emitter
│                           #   (absorbs pathland-engine)
├── pathland-protocol/      # Element 2 — Opcode engine (wire): 16-byte opcode,
│                           #   ring, arena, constants, events  (renamed pathland-opcode)
├── pathland-transport/     # Element 2 — Opcode engine (carrier): ring owner + network batch
├── pathland-render-gtk/    # Element 3 — Renderer: RenderTree decode + GTK native mapping
│                           #   (absorbs pathland-host; renamed pathland-gtk)
│
│  # Projections (host/driver roles — NOT a separate element)
├── pathland-native/        # C-ABI shim + NativeHost  ([lib] name stays "pathland_native")
├── pathland-guest/         # WASM component (browser/remote)
├── pathland-wit-host/      # wasmtime host bridge (browser/remote)
│
│  # Tool + demo
├── pathland-codegen/       # DSL generator (bin)
└── pathland-render-gtk-demo/  # demo bin (renamed pathland-gtk-demo)
```

### Rename table

| Current | New | `[lib] name` note |
|---|---|---|
| `pathland-opcode` | `pathland-protocol` | — |
| `pathland-engine` | *(merged into `pathland-view`)* | — |
| `pathland-view` | `pathland-view` (keep) | — |

Renaming the *crate* (package name) is safe; renaming the *output library* is not.

1. **Merge `pathland-engine` → `pathland-view`**

5. **Documentation sync**

Every crate must have a name that clearly shows whether it is retained ui (view), opcode engine (core) or renderer.

## Final plan: 3-element structure with view/core/render naming

### The one structural change that makes it work

Your directive (core = opcode engine = "diffs + emits") collides with a dependency cycle I flagged earlier: the diff emitter needs `view::Node`, while `view` needs the opcode constants. Merging the emitter into `core` only works if the **retained-tree types also move into `core`**:

- `pathland-view` keeps **only the DSL** (macros, `View`/`ViewModifier`, modifiers, `TapRecognizer`).
- `Node`, `Component`, `assign_ids`, `component_type_id`, `value_type_for` move into `pathland-core`, alongside the opcode format + diff emitter.

Result: `view` depends on `core`, `core` depends on nothing — the cycle disappears, and each crate name maps 1:1 to an element.

- Opcode engine → `pathland-core*`
- Renderer → `pathland-render*`

| 8 | `pathland-codegen` | Tool (bin) | unchanged |
| 9 | `pathland-render-gtk-demo` | Demo (bin) | `pathland-gtk-demo` |

### Resulting dependency graph

```
pathland-core (no deps, no_std)
├── pathland-view            (view → core)
├── pathland-core-transport  (core → core, std)
├── pathland-render-gtk      (render → core + transport)

1: //! # pathland-view
2: //!
3: //! The Pathland SwiftUI-style view DSL. Core components (`VStack`, `HStack`,
4: //! `Text`) and chainable modifiers (`spacing`, `padding`, `font_size`, `color`,
5: //! `background`) build a retained **view tree** (`Node`) that
6: //! `pathland-engine` turns into declarative `TREE`/`STYLE` opcodes.
7: //!
8: //! ## Building a tree
9: //!
10: //! Use the `vstack!`/`hstack!` macros (which box children for you) with the
11: //! free `text`/`spacer` functions, then chain modifiers and `build()`:
12: //!
13: //! ```
14: //! use pathland_view::{vstack, hstack, text, View, ViewExt};
15: //!
16: //! let node = vstack![
17: //!     text("a"),
18: //!     hstack![text("b")],
19: //! ]
20: //! .padding(16.0)
21: //! .build();
22: //! # let _ = node;
23: //! ```
24: //!
25: //! ## Decoupled modifiers
26: //!
27: //! Modifiers are **decoupled from views** (SwiftUI-style): any modifier applies
28: //! to any view via the blanket `View::modifier`, and application code composes
29: //! **custom modifiers** from the core ones by implementing `ViewModifier`:
30: //!
31: //! ```
32: //! use pathland_view::{View, ViewExt, ViewModifier, Node, Padding, Background};
33: //!
34: //! struct Card;
35: //! impl ViewModifier for Card {
36: //!     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node) {
37: //!         Padding(16.0).apply(node);
38: //!         Background(0xFF_EEEEEE).apply(node);
39: //!     }
40: //! }
41: //!

44: //! let b = pathland_view::vstack![].modifier(Card);

49: //! property and the renderer ignores what it cannot apply.

54: //! bounds; native renderers lay out their own elements.

711: /// Assign stable unique sequential ids to a tree (pre-order; root first).
712: ///
713: /// The engine keys its diff snapshot by node id, so call this after building
714: /// the (possibly re-built) tree and before `Engine::emit`.
715: pub fn assign_ids(root: &mut Node, next: &mut u32) {
716:     root.id = *next;
717:     *next += 1;
718:     for child in &mut root.children {
719:         assign_ids(child, next);
720:     }
721: }

723: /// Collect a `node id → tap callback` map from a built (and id-assigned) tree.
724: ///
725: /// Call after [`assign_ids`] so each node has its stable id; the returned map
726: /// keys the recognizer's tap target to the closure registered by
727: /// `.on_tap_gesture(...)`.
728: pub fn collect_tap_handlers(
729:     root: &Node,
730:     out: &mut BTreeMap<u32, Rc<RefCell<dyn FnMut() + 'static>>>,
731: ) {
732:     for gesture in &root.gestures {
733:         let Gesture::Tap(handler) = gesture;
734:         out.insert(root.id, handler.clone());
735:     }
736:     for child in &root.children {
737:         collect_tap_handlers(child, out);
738:     }
739: }

1: //! App-side gesture recognition over raw-input events.
2: //!
3: //! The protocol carries only raw inputs (`POINTER_DOWN` / `POINTER_UP` /
4: //! `POINTER_MOVE`, …). High-level interpretations — tap, drag, long-press — are
5: //! built by the application from those raw events. [`TapRecognizer`] is the
6: //! first such recognizer; more gestures can be added later.
7: //!
8: //! This module is `no_std`; time is supplied by the caller (`now_ms`) so the
9: //! recognizer stays independent of a platform clock.
10: 
11: use pathland_opcode::Event;
12: 
13: /// Recognizes a tap: a `POINTER_DOWN` followed by a `POINTER_UP` on the same
14: /// target, within a movement slop and a time window.
15: ///
16: /// Feed events (and a monotonic timestamp in milliseconds) to [`feed`]; it
17: /// returns `Some(target)` when a tap completes. A `POINTER_MOVE` beyond the
18: /// slop, leaving the node, or a down/up pair on different targets cancels the
19: /// gesture.
20: ///
21: /// [`feed`]: TapRecognizer::feed
22: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
23: pub struct TapRecognizer {
24:     down: Option<DownState>,
25:     /// Maximum travel (in logical points) from press to release before the
26:     /// gesture is cancelled.
27:     max_distance: f32,
28:     /// Maximum press-to-release duration in milliseconds.
29:     max_duration: u64,
30: }
31: 
32: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
33: struct DownState {
34:     target: u32,
35:     x: f32,
36:     y: f32,
37:     time: u64,
38: }
39: 
40: impl Default for TapRecognizer {
41:     fn default() -> Self {
42:         Self::new()
43:     }
44: }
45: 
46: impl TapRecognizer {
47:     /// A recognizer with default limits (10 logical points, 500 ms).
48:     pub fn new() -> Self {
49:         Self {
50:             down: None,
51:             max_distance: 10.0,
52:             max_duration: 500,
53:         }
54:     }
55: 
56:     /// A recognizer with explicit limits.
57:     pub fn with_limits(max_distance: f32, max_duration_ms: u64) -> Self {
58:         Self {
59:             down: None,
60:             max_distance,
61:             max_duration: max_duration_ms,
62:         }
63:     }
64: 
65:     /// Feed one raw-input event; returns `Some(target)` when a tap completes.
66:     pub fn feed(&mut self, event: &Event, now_ms: u64) -> Option<u32> {
67:         match event {
68:             Event::PointerDown { target, x, y, .. } => {
69:                 self.down = Some(DownState {
70:                     target: *target,
71:                     x: *x,
72:                     y: *y,
73:                     time: now_ms,
74:                 });
75:                 None
76:             }
77:             Event::PointerUp { target, x, y, .. } => {
78:                 let mut tapped = None;
79:                 if let Some(d) = self.down.take() {
80:                     if d.target == *target
81:                         && now_ms.saturating_sub(d.time) <= self.max_duration
82:                         && distance_sq(d.x, d.y, *x, *y) <= self.max_distance * self.max_distance
83:                     {
84:                         tapped = Some(*target);
85:                     }
86:                 }
87:                 tapped
88:             }
89:             Event::PointerMove {
90:                 target,
91:                 x,
92:                 y,
93:                 leaving,
94:                 ..
95:             } => {
96:                 if let Some(d) = self.down {
97:                     if *leaving
98:                         || *target != d.target
99:                         || distance_sq(d.x, d.y, *x, *y) > self.max_distance * self.max_distance
100:                     {
101:                         self.down = None;
102:                     }
103:                 }
104:                 None
105:             }
106:             _ => None,
107:         }
108:     }
109: 
110:     /// Cancel any in-progress gesture.
111:     pub fn reset(&mut self) {
112:         self.down = None;
113:     }
114: }
115: 
116: /// Squared Euclidean distance between two points (avoids `sqrt`, keeping the
117: /// module `no_std`-friendly).
118: fn distance_sq(x0: f32, y0: f32, x1: f32, y1: f32) -> f32 {
119:     let dx = x1 - x0;
120:     let dy = y1 - y0;
121:     dx * dx + dy * dy
122: }

1: //! # pathland-opcode
2: //!
3: //! The 16-byte fixed-size opcode engine for Pathland: fixed-size opcodes, a
4: //! single-producer ring buffer, a bump arena for variable-length data, and the
5: //! linear-memory layout shared with host renderers.
6: //!
7: //! This crate is `no_std` + `alloc`. It has no runtime dependencies.
8: //!
9: //! ## Producer (guest engine)
10: //!
11: //! ```no_run
12: //! use pathland_opcode::{init_memory, Guest, MemoryLayout};
13: //!
14: //! let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
15: //! let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
16: //! init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
17: //!
18: //! let mut guest = Guest::new(&mut mem, &layout);

75: /// Initialize the linear memory header for a layout. Call once at startup
76: /// before creating a `Guest` or `Host`.
77: pub fn init_memory(mem: &mut [u8], layout: &MemoryLayout) {
78:     header::init(mem, layout);
79: }
80: 
81: /// Accessor for a shared-memory ring header, for consumers that read the ring
82: /// in place (zero-copy) without a `Host` handle — e.g. a foreign driver that
83: /// holds a raw pointer to the shared linear memory.
84: ///
85: /// Field offsets match [`memory::OFF_*`] constants and are part of the stable
86: /// wire layout (see `spec/OPCODE.md`).
87: pub struct SharedHeader<'a> {
88:     mem: &'a [u8],
89: }
90: 
91: impl<'a> SharedHeader<'a> {
92:     /// Wrap an immutable view of the shared linear memory.
93:     pub fn new(mem: &'a [u8]) -> Self {
94:         Self { mem }
95:     }
96: 
97:     fn u32(&self, off: usize) -> u32 {
98:         u32::from_le_bytes(self.mem[off..off + 4].try_into().unwrap())
99:     }
100: 
101:     /// `frameCount` — the completed-frame watermark.
102:     pub fn frame_count(&self) -> u32 {
103:         self.u32(memory::OFF_FRAME_COUNT)
104:     }
105: 
106:     /// `readCursor` — the slot the consumer has consumed up to (masked).
107:     pub fn read_cursor(&self) -> u32 {
108:         self.u32(memory::OFF_READ_CURSOR)
109:     }
110: 
111:     /// `writeCursor` — the slot the producer has written up to (masked).
112:     pub fn write_cursor(&self) -> u32 {
113:         self.u32(memory::OFF_WRITE_CURSOR)
114:     }
115: 
116:     /// `slotCount` — number of ring slots (power of two).
117:     pub fn slot_count(&self) -> u32 {
118:         self.u32(memory::OFF_SLOT_COUNT)
119:     }
120: 
121:     /// Byte offset of the ring region within the linear memory.
122:     pub fn ring_offset(&self) -> usize {
123:         self.u32(memory::OFF_RING_OFFSET) as usize
124:     }
125: 
126:     /// Byte length of the ring region.
127:     pub fn ring_bytes(&self) -> usize {
128:         self.u32(memory::OFF_RING_BYTES) as usize
129:     }
130: 
131:     /// Byte offset of the arena region within the linear memory.
132:     pub fn arena_offset(&self) -> usize {
133:         self.u32(memory::OFF_ARENA_OFFSET) as usize
134:     }
135: 
136:     /// Byte offset of the arena cursor.
137:     pub fn arena_cursor(&self) -> u32 {
138:         self.u32(memory::OFF_ARENA_CURSOR)
139:     }
140: }
141: 
142: /// Number of ring slots per the header.
143: fn slot_count(header: &[u8]) -> usize {
144:     header::get_u32(header, OFF_SLOT_COUNT) as usize
145: }
146: 
147: /// Ring mask per the header (slot count is a power of two).
148: fn slot_mask(header: &[u8]) -> usize {
149:     let slots = slot_count(header);
150:     debug_assert!(slots.is_power_of_two());
151:     slots - 1
152: }

154: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
155: // Guest (producer)
156: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
157: 
158: /// Producer side: the guest engine writing opcodes and arena data into shared
159: /// linear memory. Owns the header, ring, and arena regions as disjoint slices.
160: pub struct Guest<'a> {
161:     header: &'a mut [u8],
162:     slots: &'a mut [u8],
163:     /// Host → guest event ring (guest reads raw inputs here).
164:     event_slots: &'a mut [u8],
165:     arena: &'a mut [u8],
166:     /// Write cursor captured at `begin_frame`.
167:     frame_start: u32,
168: }
169: 
170: impl<'a> Guest<'a> {
171:     /// Create a guest view over the linear memory. `init_memory` MUST have been
172:     /// called on the same memory beforehand.
173:     pub fn new(mem: &'a mut [u8], layout: &MemoryLayout) -> Self {
174:         let (header, rest) = mem.split_at_mut(memory::HEADER_SIZE);
175:         let (slots, rest) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.ring_bytes());
176:         let (event_slots, arena) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.event_ring_bytes());
177:         let frame_start = header::get_u32(header, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR);
178:         Self {
179:             header,
180:             slots,
181:             event_slots,
182:             arena,
183:             frame_start,
184:         }
185:     }
186: 
187:     fn mask(&self) -> usize {
188:         slot_mask(self.header)
189:     }
190: 
191:     /// Record the start of a new frame.
192:     pub fn begin_frame(&mut self) {
193:         self.frame_start = header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR);
194:     }
195: 
196:     /// Number of opcodes written since the last `begin_frame`.
197:     pub fn pending(&self) -> usize {
198:         let write = header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR);
199:         let mask = self.mask() as u32;
200:         (write.wrapping_sub(self.frame_start) & mask) as usize
201:     }
202: 
203:     /// End the frame: increments `frameCount`.
204:     pub fn end_frame(&mut self) {
205:         let count = header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT);
206:         header::set_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT, count.wrapping_add(1));
207:     }
208: 
209:     /// Total frames produced so far.
210:     pub fn frame_count(&self) -> u32 {
211:         header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT)
212:     }
213: 
214:     // --- TREE ---
215: 
216:     pub fn create_node(&mut self, node_id: u32, component_type: u16) -> Result<(), RingError> {
217:         ring_fn::push_create_node(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), node_id, component_type)
218:     }
219: 
220:     pub fn delete_node(&mut self, node_id: u32) -> Result<(), RingError> {
221:         ring_fn::push_delete_node(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), node_id)
222:     }
223: 
224:     pub fn insert_child(&mut self, parent: u32, child: u32, index: u32) -> Result<(), RingError> {
225:         ring_fn::push_insert_child(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), parent, child, index)
226:     }
227: 
228:     pub fn remove_child(&mut self, parent: u32, child: u32) -> Result<(), RingError> {
229:         ring_fn::push_remove_child(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), parent, child)
230:     }
231: 
232:     pub fn move_child(
233:         &mut self,
234:         parent: u32,
235:         child: u32,
236:         new_index: u32,
237:     ) -> Result<(), RingError> {
238:         ring_fn::push_move_child(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), parent, child, new_index)
239:     }
240: 
241:     // --- STYLE ---
242: 
243:     pub fn set_property(
244:         &mut self,
245:         node_id: u32,
246:         property_id: u16,
247:         value_type: u8,
248:         value: u32,
249:     ) -> Result<(), RingError> {
250:         ring_fn::push_set_property(
251:             self.slots,
252:             self.header,
253:             self.mask(),
254:             node_id,
255:             property_id,
256:             value_type,
257:             value,
258:         )
259:     }
260: 
261:     /// Set a node's text content via the arena.
262:     pub fn set_text(&mut self, node_id: u32, text: &str) -> Result<u32, RingError> {
263:         let arena_ref = arena_fn::alloc_str(self.arena, self.header, text).map_err(|_| RingError::Full)?;
264:         ring_fn::push_set_text(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), node_id, arena_ref)?;
265:         Ok(arena_ref)
266:     }
267: 
268:     /// Allocate arbitrary bytes into the arena, returning the offset.
269:     pub fn alloc(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<u32, ArenaError> {
270:         arena_fn::alloc(self.arena, self.header, bytes)
271:     }
272: 
273:     /// Allocate a string into the arena, returning the offset.
274:     pub fn alloc_str(&mut self, s: &str) -> Result<u32, ArenaError> {
275:         arena_fn::alloc_str(self.arena, self.header, s)
276:     }
277: 
278:     // --- META ---
279: 
280:     pub fn reset(&mut self) -> Result<(), RingError> {
281:         ring_fn::push_reset(self.slots, self.header, self.mask())
282:     }
283: 
284:     // --- EVENT ingress (host → guest) ---
285: 
286:     /// Drain all pending raw-input events written by the host into the event
287:     /// ring, decoding each 16-byte `EVENT` opcode into a typed [`Event`].
288:     ///
289:     /// The guest (app/engine) polls this to receive renderer-reported inputs.
290:     pub fn drain_events(&mut self) -> Vec<Event> {
291:         let mask = self.mask();
292:         let ops = ring_fn::read_events(&self.event_slots, self.header, mask);
293:         ops.into_iter()
294:             .filter_map(|op| Event::try_from(op).ok())
295:             .collect()
296:     }
297: }

299: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
300: // Host (consumer)
301: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
302: 
303: /// A completed frame produced by the guest: a sequence of opcodes plus arena
304: /// access.
305: ///
306: /// `Frame` is the **transport seam**: both the shared-memory ring (`Host`) and
307: /// network batch decoders produce frame views, so consumers such as
308: /// `RenderTree::apply_frame` work identically regardless of origin.
309: pub struct Frame<'a> {
310:     slots: &'a [u8],
311:     arena: &'a [u8],
312:     start: usize,
313:     end: usize,
314: }
315: 
316: impl<'a> Frame<'a> {
317:     /// Construct a frame view over contiguous 16-byte opcode slots plus an
318:     /// arena region (`start`/`end` are byte offsets into `slots`).
319:     ///
320:     /// Used by transport backends to produce `Frame` views over their own
321:     /// buffers; `Host` builds these internally from the ring.
322:     pub fn from_parts(slots: &'a [u8], arena: &'a [u8], start: usize, end: usize) -> Self {
323:         Self {
324:             slots,
325:             arena,
326:             start,
327:             end,
328:         }
329:     }
330: 
331:     /// Iterate the opcodes in this frame, in order.
332:     pub fn opcodes(&self) -> FrameIter<'a> {
333:         FrameIter {
334:             slots: self.slots,
335:             cursor: self.start,
336:             end: self.end,
337:         }
338:     }
339: 
340:     /// Number of opcodes in the frame.
341:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
342:         (self.end - self.start) / Opcode::SIZE
343:     }
344: 
345:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
346:         self.len() == 0
347:     }
348: 
349:     /// Read an arena entry by offset (see `Guest::alloc` / `Guest::alloc_str`).
350:     pub fn arena_get(&self, offset: u32) -> Result<&'a [u8], ArenaError> {
351:         arena_fn::get(self.arena, offset)
352:     }
353: 
354:     /// Read an arena string by offset.
355:     pub fn arena_str(&self, offset: u32) -> Result<&'a str, ArenaError> {
356:         arena_fn::get_str(self.arena, offset)
357:     }
358: 
359:     /// The full arena region (for transport serialization of arena deltas).
360:     pub fn arena(&self) -> &'a [u8] {
361:         self.arena
362:     }
363: }
364: 
365: /// Iterator over the opcodes in a `Frame`.
366: pub struct FrameIter<'a> {
367:     slots: &'a [u8],
368:     cursor: usize,
369:     end: usize,
370: }
371: 
372: impl<'a> Iterator for FrameIter<'a> {
373:     type Item = Opcode;
374: 
375:     fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Opcode> {
376:         if self.cursor >= self.end {
377:             return None;
378:         }
379:         let bytes: [u8; 16] = self.slots[self.cursor..self.cursor + 16].try_into().unwrap();
380:         self.cursor += 16;
381:         Some(Opcode::from_bytes(&bytes))
382:     }
383: }
384: 
385: /// Consumer side: the host renderer reading completed frames.
386: ///
387: /// SPSC contract: the host never reads past the producer's published
388: /// `writeCursor`, and the producer never overwrites an unconsumed `readCursor`.
389: /// If the host is slow, multiple produced frames are coalesced into one `Frame`
390: /// (opcodes remain in order); the `frameCount` simply signals "new data".
391: pub struct Host<'a> {
392:     header: &'a mut [u8],
393:     slots: &'a [u8],
394:     /// Host → guest event ring (host writes raw inputs here).
395:     event_slots: &'a mut [u8],
396:     arena: &'a [u8],
397:     /// Number of frames already consumed by this host view.
398:     consumed: u32,
399: }
400: 
401: impl<'a> Host<'a> {
402:     /// Create a host view over the linear memory.
403:     pub fn new(mem: &'a mut [u8], layout: &MemoryLayout) -> Self {
404:         let (header, rest) = mem.split_at_mut(memory::HEADER_SIZE);
405:         let (slots, rest) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.ring_bytes());
406:         let (event_slots, arena) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.event_ring_bytes());
407:         let slots: &'a [u8] = slots;
408:         let arena: &'a [u8] = arena;
409:         Self {
410:             header,
411:             slots,
412:             event_slots,
413:             arena,
414:             consumed: 0,
415:         }
416:     }
417: 
418:     /// Total frames produced by the guest (for diagnostics).
419:     pub fn frame_count(&self) -> u32 {
420:         header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT)
421:     }
422: 
423:     /// Consume all frames produced since the last call, advancing `readCursor`.
424:     ///
425:     /// Returns at most one `Frame` (all new opcodes since the last drain). If
426:     /// the producer produced multiple frames before this call they coalesce.
427:     pub fn frames(&mut self) -> Vec<Frame<'a>> {
428:         let frame_count = header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT);
429:         if self.consumed >= frame_count {
430:             return Vec::new();
431:         }
432:         let mask = slot_mask(self.header);
433:         let start = ring_fn::cursor(self.header, OFF_READ_CURSOR, mask);
434:         let end = ring_fn::cursor(self.header, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR, mask);
435: 
436:         // The POC producer flushes before the ring fills, so `end >= start`
437:         // always holds. Guard against a wrapped ring by draining nothing; a
438:         // wrapped producer must flush first (see OPCODE.md backpressure).
439:         if end < start {
440:             return Vec::new();
441:         }
442: 
443:         // No new opcodes since the last drain (readCursor == writeCursor). This
444:         // also covers a freshly-created host view whose `consumed` counter
445:         // starts at 0 but whose cursors have already been drained by an earlier
446:         // view — without this, `next_frame` would return empty frames forever.
447:         if start == end {
448:             return Vec::new();
449:         }
450: 
451:         let frames = vec![Frame {
452:             slots: self.slots,
453:             arena: self.arena,
454:             start: start * Opcode::SIZE,
455:             end: end * Opcode::SIZE,
456:         }];
457: 
458:         header::set_u32(self.header, OFF_READ_CURSOR, end as u32);
459:         self.consumed = frame_count;
460:         frames
461:     }
462: 
463:     /// Write a raw-input event (host → guest) into the event ring, encoded as a
464:     /// 16-byte `EVENT` opcode. The renderer reports inputs here; the guest
465:     /// drains them via [`Guest::drain_events`].
466:     pub fn send_event(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), RingError> {
467:         let mask = slot_mask(self.header);
468:         ring_fn::push_event(self.event_slots, self.header, mask, &event.encode())
469:     }
470: }
