1: //! # pathland-guest
2: //!
3: //! The Pathland **WASM guest component**. It owns the canonical retained view
4: //! tree and the diff-based engine, and exposes the flat, language-agnostic
5: //! `pathland:view/pathland` world:
6: //!
7: //! - **`builder`** — build/update the retained tree by node id.
8: //! - **`engine`** — frame lifecycle + `emit` (writes delta opcodes into the
9: //!   ring/arena in linear memory) and `take-batch` (returns the pending frame
10: //!   as a network batch).
11: //! - **`input`** — raw-input event ingress from the host; routed back to the
12: //!   host's `app.on-event` callback.
13: //!
14: //! Any WIT host (GTK desktop, future Java/Quarkus) drives this component; each
15: //! language wraps the world in its own ergonomic surface.
16: //!
17: //! This crate is built as a WASM component with `cargo component build
18: //! -p pathland-guest`. For the native workspace build it compiles to an empty
19: //! crate (the implementation is gated on `target_arch = "wasm32"`).
20: 
21: #![cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
22: 
23: use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap};
24: use std::sync::Mutex;
25: 
26: use pathland_engine::Engine;
27: use pathland_opcode::property_id;
28: use pathland_opcode::{init_memory, Guest as RingGuest, Host, MemoryLayout, Opcode};
29: use pathland_transport::BatchEncoder;
30: use pathland_view::Node;
31: 
32: #[allow(warnings)]
33: mod bindings;
34: 
35: use bindings::exports::pathland::view::builder::Guest as BuilderGuest;
36: use bindings::exports::pathland::view::engine::Guest as EngineGuest;
37: use bindings::exports::pathland::view::input::Guest as InputGuest;
38: use bindings::pathland::view::types::{Component, Event, Property};
39: 
40: /// A flat node in the guest's retained tree (id → node).
41: #[derive(Clone)]
42: struct FlatNode {
43:     id: u32,
44:     view_component: pathland_view::Component,
45:     properties: BTreeMap<u16, u32>,
46:     parent: Option<u32>,
47:     children: Vec<u32>,
48: }
49: 
50: /// The guest component state: retained tree, engine, ring memory.
51: ///
52: /// The WIT exports are stateless functions, so state lives in a global mutex
53: /// (the component model is single-threaded per instance; a plain `static`
54: /// would also work, but `Mutex` keeps the borrow checker happy).
55: struct State {
56:     nodes: HashMap<u32, FlatNode>,
57:     engine: Engine,
58:     mem: Vec<u8>,
59:     layout: MemoryLayout,
60:     encoder: BatchEncoder,
61: }
62: 
63: static STATE: Mutex<Option<State>> = Mutex::new(None);
64: 
65: fn state() -> &'static Mutex<Option<State>> {
66:     &STATE
67: }
68: 
69: /// Initialize the guest state (idempotent).
70: fn ensure_state() {
71:     let mut guard = state().lock().unwrap();
72:     if guard.is_none() {
73:         let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
74:         let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
75:         init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
76:         *guard = Some(State {
77:             nodes: HashMap::new(),
78:             engine: Engine::new(),
79:             mem,
80:             layout,
81:             encoder: BatchEncoder::new(),
82:         });
83:     }
84: }
85: 
86: /// Map a WIT component to a `pathland_view::Component`.
87: fn to_view_component(c: &Component) -> pathland_view::Component {
88:     match c {
89:         Component::Hstack => pathland_view::Component::HStack,
90:         Component::Vstack => pathland_view::Component::VStack,
91:         Component::Text => pathland_view::Component::Text { text: String::new() },
92:         Component::Button => pathland_view::Component::Button { label: String::new() },
93:         Component::Spacer => pathland_view::Component::Spacer,
94:     }
95: }
96: 
97: /// Map a WIT property to a protocol property id.
98: fn to_property_id(p: &Property) -> u16 {
99:     match p {
100:         Property::Spacing => property_id::SPACING,
101:         Property::Padding => property_id::PADDING,
102:         Property::FontSize => property_id::FONT_SIZE,
103:         Property::Color => property_id::COLOR,
104:         Property::BackgroundColor => property_id::BACKGROUND_COLOR,
105:     }
106: }
107: 
108: /// Materialize a `pathland_view::Node` tree rooted at `root_id`, pre-order.
109: fn materialize(nodes: &HashMap<u32, FlatNode>, root_id: u32) -> Option<Node> {
110:     let flat = nodes.get(&root_id)?.clone();
111:     let mut node = Node::from_component(&flat.view_component);
112:     node.id = flat.id;
113:     node.properties = flat.properties.clone();
114:     for child_id in &flat.children {
115:         if let Some(child) = materialize(nodes, *child_id) {
116:             node.children.push(child);
117:         }
118:     }
119:     Some(node)
120: }
121: 
122: /// The root is the node without a parent (the app authors a single root).
123: fn root_id(nodes: &HashMap<u32, FlatNode>) -> Option<u32> {
124:     nodes
125:         .values()
126:         .find(|n| n.parent.is_none())
127:         .map(|n| n.id)
128: }
129: 
130: impl BuilderGuest for State {
131:     fn create_node(id: u32, component: Component) {
132:         ensure_state();
133:         let mut guard = state().lock().unwrap();
134:         let s = guard.as_mut().unwrap();
135:         let entry = s.nodes.entry(id).or_insert(FlatNode {
136:             id,
137:             view_component: to_view_component(&component),
138:             properties: BTreeMap::new(),
139:             parent: None,
140:             children: Vec::new(),
141:         });
142:         entry.view_component = to_view_component(&component);
143:         entry.properties.clear();
144:     }
145: 
146:     fn insert_child(parent: u32, child: u32, index: u32) {
147:         ensure_state();
148:         let mut guard = state().lock().unwrap();
149:         let s = guard.as_mut().unwrap();
150:         if let Some(p) = s.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
151:             let idx = if index == u32::MAX {
152:                 p.children.len()
153:             } else {
154:                 (index as usize).min(p.children.len())
155:             };
156:             if !p.children.contains(&child) {
157:                 p.children.insert(idx, child);
158:             }
159:         }
160:         if let Some(c) = s.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
161:             c.parent = Some(parent);
162:         }
163:     }
164: 
165:     fn remove_child(parent: u32, child: u32) {
166:         ensure_state();
167:         let mut guard = state().lock().unwrap();
168:         let s = guard.as_mut().unwrap();
169:         if let Some(p) = s.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
170:             p.children.retain(|c| *c != child);
171:         }
172:         if let Some(c) = s.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
173:             c.parent = None;
174:         }
175:     }
176: 
177:     fn set_text(id: u32, text: String) {
178:         ensure_state();
179:         let mut guard = state().lock().unwrap();
180:         let s = guard.as_mut().unwrap();
181:         if let Some(node) = s.nodes.get_mut(&id) {
182:             match &mut node.view_component {
183:                 pathland_view::Component::Text { text: t } => *t = text,
184:                 pathland_view::Component::Button { label } => *label = text,
185:                 _ => {}
186:             }
187:         }
188:     }
189: 
190:     fn set_property(id: u32, property: Property, value: f32) {
191:         ensure_state();
192:         let mut guard = state().lock().unwrap();
193:         let s = guard.as_mut().unwrap();
194:         if let Some(node) = s.nodes.get_mut(&id) {
195:             let pid = to_property_id(&property);
196:             if property == Property::Color || property == Property::BackgroundColor {
197:                 node.properties.insert(pid, value as u32);
198:             } else {
199:                 node.properties.insert(pid, value.to_bits());
200:             }
201:         }
202:     }
203: }
204: 
205: impl EngineGuest for State {
206:     fn begin_frame() {
207:         ensure_state();
208:     }
209: 
210:     fn emit() {
211:         ensure_state();
212:         let mut guard = state().lock().unwrap();
213:         let s = guard.as_mut().unwrap();
214:         let root = root_id(&s.nodes).and_then(|r| materialize(&s.nodes, r));
215:         if let Some(root) = root {
216:             let mut ring = RingGuest::new(&mut s.mem, &s.layout);
217:             ring.begin_frame();
218:             s.engine.emit(&root, &mut ring).ok();
219:             ring.end_frame();
220:         }
221:     }
222: 
223:     fn end_frame() {}
224: 
225:     fn take_batch() -> Vec<u8> {
226:         ensure_state();
227:         let mut guard = state().lock().unwrap();
228:         let s = guard.as_mut().unwrap();
229:         // Drain completed frames from the ring and encode them as a batch.
230:         let mut host = Host::new(&mut s.mem, &s.layout);
231:         let mut bytes = Vec::new();
232:         for frame in host.frames() {
233:             let opcodes: Vec<Opcode> = frame.opcodes().collect();
234:             let arena = frame.arena().to_vec();
235:             let frame_count = host.frame_count();
236:             bytes.extend(s.encoder.encode(frame_count, &opcodes, &arena));
237:         }
238:         bytes
239:     }
240: }
241: 
242: impl InputGuest for State {
243:     fn dispatch(event: Event) {
244:         route_event(event);
245:     }
246: }

249: fn route_event(event: Event) {
250:     bindings::pathland::view::app::on_event(event);
251: }

1: //! # pathland-wit-host
2: //!
3: //! Host-side bindings for the `pathland:view/pathland` world plus a **DSL
4: //! bridge**: instantiate the compiled `pathland-guest` component in wasmtime
5: //! and drive its flat `builder` interface from a `pathland_view::Node` tree.
6: //!
7: //! The bridge is what makes the DSL a uniform surface: a developer authors a
8: //! tree with `vstack![...]` / `text(...)` / custom views, and this crate walks
9: //! that `Node` tree and issues the equivalent WIT `builder` calls. Custom views
10: //! and core views are indistinguishable here — both resolve to the same `Node`
11: //! tree.
12: 
13: use pathland_opcode::property_id;
14: use pathland_view::Node;
15: use wasmtime::component::bindgen;
16: use wasmtime::component::{HasSelf, ResourceTable};
17: use wasmtime::{Config, Engine, Store};
18: use wasmtime_wasi::p2::add_to_linker_sync as add_wasi_to_linker;
19: use wasmtime_wasi::{WasiCtx, WasiCtxBuilder, WasiCtxView, WasiView};
20: 
21: // Component bindings for the `pathland:view/pathland` world.
22: bindgen!({
23:     world: "pathland",
24:     path: "../../../../wit",
25: });
26: 
27: pub use pathland::view::types::{self as types, Component, Event, Property};
28: 
29: /// Errors produced while driving the guest component.
30: #[derive(Debug)]
31: pub enum HostError {
32:     /// wasmtime failed to instantiate or run the component.
33:     Wasmtime(wasmtime::Error),
34: }
35: 
36: impl From<wasmtime::Error> for HostError {
37:     fn from(e: wasmtime::Error) -> Self {
38:         HostError::Wasmtime(e)
39:     }
40: }
41: 
42: /// The application callback provided by the host (the guest's `app.on-event`).
43: ///
44: /// The `&mut Store<App>` is passed so the handler can reach host state (e.g.
45: /// rebuild the DSL tree and re-emit).
46: pub trait AppHandler: Send {
47:     /// Handle a raw input routed back from the guest.
48:     fn on_event(&mut self, event: &Event);
49: }
50: 
51: /// A null handler for tests that don't need event routing.
52: pub struct NullApp;
53: 
54: impl AppHandler for NullApp {
55:     fn on_event(&mut self, _event: &Event) {}
56: }
57: 
58: /// The host application type is the guest's `app` import.
59: ///
60: /// `add_to_linker` requires the store data type to implement the `Host` trait;
61: /// we blanket-forward to the `AppHandler` trait.
62: impl pathland::view::types::Host for AppHost {}
63: impl pathland::view::app::Host for AppHost {
64:     fn on_event(&mut self, event: Event) {
65:         AppHandler::on_event(self.app.as_mut(), &event);
66:     }
67: }
68: 
69: /// Host-side store state: the app handler plus WASI (the wasip1 guest imports
70: /// the WASI reactor interfaces even though Pathland itself doesn't use them).
71: pub struct AppHost {
72:     app: Box<dyn AppHandler>,
73:     wasi: WasiCtx,
74:     table: ResourceTable,
75: }
76: 
77: impl WasiView for AppHost {
78:     fn ctx(&mut self) -> WasiCtxView<'_> {
79:         WasiCtxView {
80:             ctx: &mut self.wasi,
81:             table: &mut self.table,
82:         }
83:     }
84: }
85: 
86: /// A ready-to-drive guest component: the wasmtime store + instance.
87: pub struct GuestHost {
88:     store: Store<AppHost>,
89:     pathland: Pathland,
90: }
91: 
92: impl GuestHost {
93:     /// Instantiate the compiled `pathland-guest` component.
94:     pub fn new(component_bytes: &[u8], app: impl AppHandler + 'static) -> Result<Self, HostError> {
95:         let mut config = Config::new();
96:         config.wasm_component_model(true);
97:         let engine = Engine::new(&config)?;
98:         let mut store = Store::new(
99:             &engine,
100:             AppHost {
101:                 app: Box::new(app),
102:                 wasi: WasiCtxBuilder::new().build(),
103:                 table: ResourceTable::new(),
104:             },
105:         );
106: 
107:         let component = wasmtime::component::Component::new(&engine, component_bytes)?;
108:         let mut linker = wasmtime::component::Linker::new(&engine);
109:         // The guest imports the WASI preview1 reactor interfaces (from the
110:         // wasip1 target); satisfy them with the component-model WASI host.
111:         add_wasi_to_linker::<AppHost>(&mut linker)?;
112:         // The guest calls back into the host via `pathland:view/app/on-event`.
113:         pathland::view::app::add_to_linker::<_, HasSelf<_>>(&mut linker, |x| x)?;
114:         let pathland = Pathland::instantiate(&mut store, &component, &linker)?;
115: 
116:         Ok(Self { store, pathland })
117:     }
118: 
119:     /// The store's app handler (used after `dispatch` to let the host react).
120:     pub fn app(&mut self) -> &mut dyn AppHandler {
121:         self.store.data_mut().app.as_mut()
122:     }
123: 
124:     /// Run the bridge: walk a DSL `Node` tree into the guest's retained tree.
125:     ///
126:     /// The tree's node ids (from `assign_ids`) become the guest's stable ids,
127:     /// so re-sending an updated tree lets the guest diff and emit only deltas.
128:     pub fn import_tree(&mut self, root: &Node) -> Result<(), HostError> {
129:         import_tree(&mut self.pathland, &mut self.store, root)?;
130:         Ok(())
131:     }
132: 
133:     /// Emit the retained tree as a network batch (opcodes + arena delta).
134:     pub fn emit(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, HostError> {
135:         let builder = self.pathland.pathland_view_engine();
136:         builder.call_begin_frame(&mut self.store)?;
137:         builder.call_emit(&mut self.store)?;
138:         builder.call_end_frame(&mut self.store)?;
139:         let bytes = builder.call_take_batch(&mut self.store)?;
140:         Ok(bytes)
141:     }
142: 
143:     /// Dispatch a raw input into the guest (routed back via `app.on-event`).
144:     pub fn dispatch(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), HostError> {
145:         let input = self.pathland.pathland_view_input();
146:         input.call_dispatch(&mut self.store, *event)?;
147:         Ok(())
148:     }
149: }
150: 
151: /// Map a `pathland_view::Component` to the WIT `Component` variant.
152: fn to_wit_component(c: &pathland_view::Component) -> Component {
153:     match c {
154:         pathland_view::Component::VStack => Component::Vstack,
155:         pathland_view::Component::HStack => Component::Hstack,
156:         pathland_view::Component::Text { .. } => Component::Text,
157:         pathland_view::Component::Button { .. } => Component::Button,
158:         pathland_view::Component::Spacer => Component::Spacer,
159:     }
160: }
161: 
162: /// Map a protocol property id to the WIT `Property` variant.
163: fn to_wit_property(pid: u16) -> Option<Property> {
164:     match pid {
165:         property_id::SPACING => Some(Property::Spacing),
166:         property_id::PADDING => Some(Property::Padding),
167:         property_id::FONT_SIZE => Some(Property::FontSize),
168:         property_id::COLOR => Some(Property::Color),
169:         property_id::BACKGROUND_COLOR => Some(Property::BackgroundColor),
170:         _ => None,
171:     }
172: }
173: 
174: /// Walk a DSL `Node` tree into the guest's flat retained tree via WIT builder
175: /// calls. Pre-order: create each node, then set text/properties, then children.
176: pub fn import_tree(
177:     pathland: &mut Pathland,
178:     store: &mut Store<AppHost>,
179:     root: &Node,
180: ) -> Result<(), HostError> {
181:     let builder = pathland.pathland_view_builder();
182:     import_node(builder, store, root)?;
183:     Ok(())
184: }
185: 
186: fn import_node(
187:     builder: &exports::pathland::view::builder::Guest,
188:     store: &mut Store<AppHost>,
189:     node: &Node,
190: ) -> Result<(), HostError> {
191:     builder.call_create_node(&mut *store, node.id, to_wit_component(&node.component))?;
192:     match &node.component {
193:         pathland_view::Component::Text { text } => {
194:             builder.call_set_text(&mut *store, node.id, text.as_str())?;
195:         }
196:         pathland_view::Component::Button { label } => {
197:             builder.call_set_text(&mut *store, node.id, label.as_str())?;
198:         }
199:         _ => {}
200:     }
201:     for (pid, value) in &node.properties {
202:         if let Some(prop) = to_wit_property(*pid) {
203:             let f = match *pid {
204:                 property_id::COLOR | property_id::BACKGROUND_COLOR => *value as f32,
205:                 _ => f32::from_bits(*value),
206:             };
207:             builder.call_set_property(&mut *store, node.id, prop, f)?;
208:         }
209:     }
210:     // Children must exist before insertion (so the guest can link them).
211:     for child in &node.children {
212:         import_node(builder, store, child)?;
213:         builder.call_insert_child(&mut *store, node.id, child.id, u32::MAX)?;
214:     }
215:     Ok(())
216: }

1: //! C ABI for the Pathland native host.
2: //!
3: //! Foreign host languages (Swift, Java, C#, …) link this `cdylib` and call the
4: //! `pathland_native_*` functions. The surface is the **flat world** — no
5: //! per-component wrappers — and the ring is exposed as a raw pointer + length so
6: //! the foreign driver reads opcodes **in place** (zero-copy).
7: //!
8: //! ```c
9: //! void* h = pathland_native_create();
10: //! pathland_native_create_node(h, 1, 2);            // 2 = vstack
11: //! pathland_native_create_node(h, 2, 3);            // 3 = text
12: //! pathland_native_set_text(h, 2, "Hello");
13: //! pathland_native_insert_child(h, 1, 2, UINT32_MAX);
14: //! pathland_native_emit(h);
15: //! // read opcodes from pathland_native_ring_ptr(h) (header at offset 0)
16: //! pathland_native_destroy(h);
17: //! ```
18: 
19: use std::ffi::{c_char, c_void, CStr};
20: 
21: use super::{component_from_id, NativeHost};
22: 
23: /// Opaque handle to a [`NativeHost`].
24: pub type HostHandle = *mut c_void;
25: 
26: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
27: // Lifetime
28: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
29: 
30: /// Create a native host over a fresh zero-copy shared ring. Returns an opaque
31: /// handle (non-null on success).
32: #[no_mangle]
33: pub extern "C" fn pathland_native_create() -> HostHandle {
34:     let host = Box::new(NativeHost::new());
35:     Box::into_raw(host) as HostHandle
36: }
37: 
38: /// Destroy a native host previously created by [`pathland_native_create`].
39: #[no_mangle]
40: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_destroy(host: HostHandle) {
41:     if !host.is_null() {
42:         drop(Box::from_raw(host as *mut NativeHost));
43:     }
44: }
45: 
46: fn as_host<'a>(host: HostHandle) -> &'a mut NativeHost {
47:     unsafe { &mut *(host as *mut NativeHost) }
48: }
49: 
50: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
51: // Flat builder (variants as raw u32)
52: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
53: 
54: /// `component_id` here is the raw protocol component id (hstack=1, vstack=2,
55: /// text=3, button=4, spacer=8). Returns 1 on success, 0 on bad component.
56: #[no_mangle]
57: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_create_node(
58:     host: HostHandle,
59:     id: u32,
60:     component: u32,
61: ) -> u8 {
62:     let Some(component) = component_from_id(component) else {
63:         return 0;
64:     };
65:     as_host(host).create_node(id, component);
66:     1
67: }
68: 
69: #[no_mangle]
70: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_insert_child(
71:     host: HostHandle,
72:     parent: u32,
73:     child: u32,
74:     index: u32,
75: ) -> u8 {
76:     as_host(host).insert_child(parent, child, index);
77:     1
78: }
79: 
80: #[no_mangle]
81: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_remove_child(host: HostHandle, parent: u32, child: u32) -> u8 {
82:     as_host(host).remove_child(parent, child);
83:     1
84: }
85: 
86: /// Set a node's text content from a NUL-terminated UTF-8 C string.
87: #[no_mangle]
88: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_set_text(
89:     host: HostHandle,
90:     id: u32,
91:     text: *const c_char,
92: ) -> u8 {
93:     if text.is_null() {
94:         return 0;
95:     }
96:     let text = CStr::from_ptr(text).to_string_lossy().into_owned();
97:     as_host(host).set_text(id, &text);
98:     1
99: }
100: 
101: /// Set a property with a raw u32 value (bit pattern — floats are passed via
102: /// `pathland_native_set_property_f32`).
103: #[no_mangle]
104: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_set_property(
105:     host: HostHandle,
106:     id: u32,
107:     prop: u32,
108:     value: u32,
109: ) -> u8 {
110:     as_host(host).set_property(id, prop as u16, value);
111:     1
112: }
113: 
114: /// Set a float-valued property.
115: #[no_mangle]
116: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_set_property_f32(
117:     host: HostHandle,
118:     id: u32,
119:     prop: u32,
120:     value: f32,
121: ) -> u8 {
122:     as_host(host).set_property_f32(id, prop as u16, value);
123:     1
124: }
125: 
126: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
127: // Engine
128: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
129: 
130: /// Emit the retained tree as opcodes into the shared ring. Returns 1 if a frame
131: /// was written.
132: #[no_mangle]
133: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_emit(host: HostHandle) -> u8 {
134:     if as_host(host).emit() {
135:         1
136:     } else {
137:         0
138:     }
139: }
140: 
141: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
142: // Zero-copy ring access
143: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
144: 
145: /// Return a pointer to the shared linear memory (header | ring | arena) so a
146: /// foreign driver can read opcodes in place. Never null; the header layout is
147: /// the stable wire layout in `spec/OPCODE.md` (frameCount/readCursor/
148: /// writeCursor/ringOffset/arenaOffset at their documented offsets).
149: #[no_mangle]
150: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_ring_ptr(host: HostHandle) -> *const u8 {
151:     let host = as_host(host);
152:     host.ring_buffer().as_ptr()
153: }
154: 
155: /// Total length in bytes of the shared linear memory buffer.
156: #[no_mangle]
157: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_ring_len(host: HostHandle) -> usize {
158:     let host = as_host(host);
159:     host.ring_buffer().len()
160: }
161: 
162: /// Convenience: return the total buffer length of the default layout.
163: #[no_mangle]
164: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_layout_bytes(host: HostHandle) -> usize {
165:     let host = as_host(host);
166:     host.layout().total_bytes()
167: }
168: 
169: /// Read the root node id (u32_MAX = none).
170: #[no_mangle]
171: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_root_id(host: HostHandle) -> u32 {
172:     as_host(host).root_id().unwrap_or(u32::MAX)
173: }
174: 
175: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
176: // Raw-input events (host → guest)
177: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
178: 
179: /// Drain pending raw-input events written by a renderer into the host → guest
180: /// event ring, writing each as its raw 16-byte `EVENT` opcode
181: /// (`[category][command][flags:u16][A:u32][B:u32][C:u32]`, little-endian) into
182: /// `out`. Returns the number of events written (≤ `max`).
183: ///
184: /// `out` must point to at least `max * 16` writable bytes. This is the generic
185: /// event path: the renderer only writes `EVENT` opcodes; the host drains them
186: /// here, symmetric with how a driver reads frame opcodes via
187: /// [`pathland_native_ring_ptr`].
188: #[no_mangle]
189: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_drain_events(
190:     host: HostHandle,
191:     out: *mut u8,
192:     max: u32,
193: ) -> u32 {
194:     if out.is_null() || max == 0 {
195:         return 0;
196:     }
197:     let events = as_host(host).drain_events();
198:     let n = events.len().min(max as usize);
199:     for (i, ev) in events.into_iter().take(n).enumerate() {
200:         let bytes = ev.encode().to_bytes();
201:         // SAFETY: `out` points to ≥ max*16 writable bytes; we write ≤ max slots.
202:         std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(bytes.as_ptr(), out.add(i * 16), 16);
203:     }
204:     n as u32
205: }

1: //! C ABI for the Pathland GTK renderer (Java host).
2: //!
3: //! A foreign host (Java via JNA) drives the `pathland-native` flat world to
4: //! build/emit the retained tree, then calls `pathland_gtk_run` to hand the
5: //! renderer its shared ring and run GTK in-process. Raw-input events are
6: //! reported back through a C callback (`void (*)(u32 targetId)`).
7: 
8: use std::cell::RefCell;
9: use std::ffi::c_void;
10: use std::rc::Rc;
11: 
12: use pathland_native::NativeHost;
13: use pathland_opcode::Event;
14: use pathland_transport::{DriverTransport, FrameSource, OpcodeBatch, TransportError};
15: 
16: use crate::{run_with_pump, Pump};
17: 
18: /// A host-supplied event callback, invoked (with no payload) when the renderer
19: /// has written a raw input into the host → guest event ring. The host drains the
20: /// ring itself (via `pathland_native_drain_events`) to receive the events.
21: pub type EventCallback = extern "C" fn();
22: 
23: /// A `Pump` over a `pathland-native` `NativeHost` owned by the foreign host.
24: ///
25: /// The renderer borrows the host through a raw pointer for the duration of
26: /// `pathland_gtk_run`; the foreign host keeps driving the same host (via its
27: /// own handle) from the event callback. All access is on the GTK main thread.
28: struct NativeHostHandle(*mut NativeHost);
29: 
30: impl Pump for NativeHostHandle {
31:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError> {
32:         // SAFETY: single-threaded (GTK main thread); the foreign host must not
33:         // destroy the host until `pathland_gtk_run` returns.
34:         unsafe { FrameSource::next_frame(&mut *self.0) }
35:     }
36: 
37:     fn send_input(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
38:         // SAFETY: as above.
39:         unsafe { DriverTransport::send_input(&mut *self.0, event) }
40:     }
41: }
42: 
43: /// Run the GTK renderer over a `pathland-native` host's shared ring.
44: ///
45: /// `host` is the opaque handle from `pathland_native_create`; the renderer
46: /// pumps its ring in-process (frames in, events out). `on_event` is called
47: /// (on the GTK main thread, with no payload) whenever a raw input was written;
48: /// the host then drains the event ring via `pathland_native_drain_events` and
49: /// may re-enter `pathland_native_*` to update the tree and re-emit.
50: ///
51: /// This function blocks until the GTK main loop exits (window closed).
52: #[no_mangle]
53: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_gtk_run(
54:     host: *mut c_void,
55:     on_event: Option<EventCallback>,
56: ) {
57:     if host.is_null() {
58:         return;
59:     }
60: 
61:     let handle = NativeHostHandle(host as *mut NativeHost);
62:     let pump = Rc::new(RefCell::new(handle));
63: 
64:     // Pass a bare program name to GTK: the real process argv is the JVM's
65:     // (`-cp`/`-D` flags + main class), which GTK must not parse as its own
66:     // options. A single non-option argument avoids both the "unknown option"
67:     // error and the empty-argv activation quirk on macOS.
68:     run_with_pump(
69:         "org.pathland.GtkDemo",
70:         "Pathland GTK Demo",
71:         pump,
72:         &["GtkDemo"],
73:         move |_pump| {
74:             if let Some(cb) = on_event {
75:                 cb();
76:             }
77:         },
78:     );
79: }

1: //! Pure opcode -> layout-decision mapping for stacks.
2: //!
3: //! This module is **display-free**: it translates a host node's component type
4: //! and constraint properties (`SPACING`, `ALIGNMENT`, `PADDING`, per-edge
5: //! padding) into plain data (`Orientation`, spacing, cross-axis `gtk::Align`,
6: //! margins) that the GTK layer then applies to native widgets.
7: //!
8: //! `gtk::Align`/`Orientation` are plain enums, not widgets, so none of this
9: //! needs GTK initialized - which keeps the mapping unit-testable headlessly.
10: 
11: use gtk::{Align, Orientation};
12: use pathland_host::HostNode;
13: use pathland_opcode::{component_type, property_id};
14: 
15: /// Map a component type to its native stack orientation.
16: pub fn stack_orientation(component_type: u16) -> Option<Orientation> {
17:     match component_type {
18:         component_type::VSTACK => Some(Orientation::Vertical),
19:         component_type::HSTACK => Some(Orientation::Horizontal),
20:         _ => None,
21:     }
22: }
23: 
24: /// The native layout a stack node maps onto.
25: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
26: pub struct StackLayout {
27:     pub orientation: Orientation,
28:     pub spacing: i32,
29:     pub child_align: Align,
30: }
31: 
32: /// Compute the stack layout from a node's component type + properties.
33: ///
34: /// Returns `None` for non-stack components. Defaults (absent properties):
35: /// spacing `0`, cross-axis alignment `Fill`.
36: pub fn stack_layout(node: &HostNode) -> Option<StackLayout> {
37:     let orientation = stack_orientation(node.component_type)?;
38:     let spacing = f32_prop(node, property_id::SPACING)
39:         .map(round_nonneg)
40:         .unwrap_or(0);
41:     let child_align = node
42:         .properties
43:         .get(&property_id::ALIGNMENT)
44:         .map(|raw| align_from(*raw))
45:         .unwrap_or(Align::Fill);
46:     Some(StackLayout {
47:         orientation,
48:         spacing,
49:         child_align,
50:     })
51: }
52: 
53: /// Whether the cross axis is horizontal (a vertical stack aligns its children
54: /// horizontally, via `halign`); `false` means vertical (a horizontal stack
55: /// aligns children via `valign`).
56: pub fn cross_axis_is_horizontal(orientation: Orientation) -> bool {
57:     orientation == Orientation::Vertical
58: }
59: 
60: /// Interpret an `ALIGNMENT` property value as a cross-axis `gtk::Align`.
61: ///
62: /// Both DSLs emit the enum index as an f32 bit pattern (`0.0..=3.0`); a raw
63: /// low-byte ENUM encoding is also accepted for robustness. Out-of-range values
64: /// fall back to `Fill`.
65: pub fn align_from(raw: u32) -> Align {
66:     let f = f32::from_bits(raw);
67:     let idx = if f.is_finite() && f.fract() == 0.0 && (0.0..=3.0).contains(&f) {
68:         f as u8
69:     } else {
70:         (raw & 0xFF) as u8
71:     };
72:     match idx {
73:         0 => Align::Start,
74:         1 => Align::Center,
75:         2 => Align::End,
76:         _ => Align::Fill,
77:     }
78: }
79: 
80: /// Per-edge padding, in logical pixels (rounded, non-negative).
81: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
82: pub struct Edges {
83:     pub top: i32,
84:     pub right: i32,
85:     pub bottom: i32,
86:     pub left: i32,
87: }
88: 
89: impl Edges {
90:     /// True when every edge is zero.
91:     pub fn is_zero(&self) -> bool {
92:         self.top == 0 && self.right == 0 && self.bottom == 0 && self.left == 0
93:     }
94: }
95: 
96: /// Compute a node's padding margins. Uniform `PADDING` sets all four edges;
97: /// per-edge `PADDING_TOP/RIGHT/BOTTOM/LEFT` override individual edges.
98: ///
99: /// Padding is **styling** (a DSL modifier), so it applies to any node, not just
100: /// stacks.
101: pub fn padding_from(node: &HostNode) -> Edges {
102:     let uniform = f32_prop(node, property_id::PADDING)
103:         .map(round_nonneg)
104:         .unwrap_or(0);
105:     Edges {
106:         top: f32_prop(node, property_id::PADDING_TOP)
107:             .map(round_nonneg)
108:             .unwrap_or(uniform),
109:         right: f32_prop(node, property_id::PADDING_RIGHT)
110:             .map(round_nonneg)
111:             .unwrap_or(uniform),
112:         bottom: f32_prop(node, property_id::PADDING_BOTTOM)
113:             .map(round_nonneg)
114:             .unwrap_or(uniform),
115:         left: f32_prop(node, property_id::PADDING_LEFT)
116:             .map(round_nonneg)
117:             .unwrap_or(uniform),
118:     }
119: }
120: 
121: fn f32_prop(node: &HostNode, prop: u16) -> Option<f32> {
122:     node.properties.get(&prop).map(|bits| f32::from_bits(*bits))
123: }
124: 
125: fn round_nonneg(f: f32) -> i32 {
126:     f.max(0.0).round() as i32
127: }

1: //! # pathland-codegen
2: //!
3: //! The **Catalog-Driven DSL generator**. It reads the single source of truth at
4: //! `lib/ui/components.yaml`, asserts every component/property id against
5: //! `pathland_opcode::constants` (a hard error on mismatch — the consistency
6: //! safety net), and emits the checked-in SwiftUI-like DSL for each target
7: //! language (currently Java).
8: //!
9: //! ## Usage
10: //!
11: //! ```sh
12: //! cargo run -p pathland-codegen
13: //! ```
14: //!
15: //! The generator is deterministic: given the same catalog it writes identical
16: //! output, so the emitted files are safe to check in.
17: 
18: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
19: use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
20: 
21: use pathland_opcode::{component_type, property_id, size};
22: 
23: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
24: // YAML model
25: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
26: 
27: #[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
28: struct Catalog {
29:     component_ids: BTreeMap<String, u16>,
30:     property_ids: BTreeMap<String, u16>,
31:     enums: BTreeMap<String, EnumDef>,
32:     components: BTreeMap<String, ComponentDef>,
33:     modifiers: Vec<ModifierDef>,
34:     #[allow(dead_code)] // frame compound modifier is emitted by emit_frame
35:     compound_modifiers: BTreeMap<String, CompoundDef>,
36: }
37: 
38: #[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
39: struct EnumDef {
40:     property: String,
41:     values: BTreeMap<String, u8>,
42: }
43: 
44: #[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
45: struct ComponentDef {
46:     label: String,
47:     #[serde(default)]
48:     text_content: bool,
49:     #[serde(default)]
50:     children: bool,
51:     #[serde(default)]
52:     constructor_props: Vec<ConstructorProp>,
53: }
54: 
55: #[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
56: struct ConstructorProp {
57:     property: String,
58:     #[serde(rename = "type")]
59:     ty: String,
60:     #[serde(default)]
61:     r#enum: Option<String>,
62: }

65: struct ModifierDef {

67:     #[serde(rename = "type")]
68:     ty: String,
69:     #[serde(default)]
70:     r#enum: Option<String>,
71: }

73: #[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
74: struct CompoundDef {
75:     #[allow(dead_code)]
76:     properties: Vec<ModifierDef>,
77: }

83: fn assert_ids(catalog: &Catalog) -> Vec<String> {
84:     let mut errors = Vec::new();
85: 
86:     let expected_components: &[(&str, u16)] = &[
87:         ("hstack", component_type::HSTACK),
88:         ("vstack", component_type::VSTACK),
89:         ("text", component_type::TEXT),
90:         ("button", component_type::BUTTON),
91:         ("image", component_type::IMAGE),
92:         ("switch", component_type::SWITCH),
93:         ("text_field", component_type::TEXT_FIELD),
94:         ("spacer", component_type::SPACER),
95:         ("scrollview", component_type::SCROLLVIEW),
96:         ("list", component_type::LIST),
97:         ("grid", component_type::GRID),
98:         ("comment", component_type::COMMENT),
99:     ];
100:     for (name, id) in expected_components {
101:         match catalog.component_ids.get(*name) {
102:             Some(cid) if cid == id => {}
103:             Some(cid) => errors.push(format!(
104:                 "component `{name}`: catalog 0x{cid:04x} != protocol 0x{id:04x}"
105:             )),
106:             None => errors.push(format!("component `{name}` missing from catalog")),
107:         }
108:     }
109: 
110:     let expected_props: &[(&str, u16)] = &[
111:         ("spacing", property_id::SPACING),
112:         ("alignment", property_id::ALIGNMENT),
113:         ("padding", property_id::PADDING),
114:         ("content_margins", property_id::CONTENT_MARGINS),
115:         ("text", property_id::TEXT),
116:         ("line_limit", property_id::LINE_LIMIT),
117:         ("text_alignment", property_id::TEXT_ALIGNMENT),
118:         ("truncation_mode", property_id::TRUNCATION_MODE),
119:         ("background_color", property_id::BACKGROUND_COLOR),
120:         ("border_width", property_id::BORDER_WIDTH),
121:         ("border_color", property_id::BORDER_COLOR),
122:         ("border_radius", property_id::BORDER_RADIUS),
123:         ("padding_style", property_id::PADDING_STYLE),
124:         ("font_size", property_id::FONT_SIZE),
125:         ("font_weight", property_id::FONT_WEIGHT),
126:         ("font_family", property_id::FONT_FAMILY),
127:         ("color", property_id::COLOR),
128:         ("width", property_id::WIDTH),
129:         ("height", property_id::HEIGHT),
130:         ("opacity", property_id::OPACITY),
131:         ("visible", property_id::VISIBLE),
132:         ("z_index", property_id::Z_INDEX),
133:         ("clips_to_bounds", property_id::CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS),
134:         ("padding_top", property_id::PADDING_TOP),
135:         ("padding_right", property_id::PADDING_RIGHT),
136:         ("padding_bottom", property_id::PADDING_BOTTOM),
137:         ("padding_left", property_id::PADDING_LEFT),
138:         ("role", property_id::ROLE),
139:         ("state", property_id::STATE),
140:         ("enabled", property_id::ENABLED),
141:         ("selected", property_id::SELECTED),
142:         ("event_listeners", property_id::EVENT_LISTENERS),
143:     ];
144:     for (name, id) in expected_props {
145:         match catalog.property_ids.get(*name) {
146:             Some(pid) if pid == id => {}
147:             Some(pid) => errors.push(format!(
148:                 "property `{name}`: catalog 0x{pid:04x} != protocol 0x{id:04x}"
149:             )),
150:             None => errors.push(format!("property `{name}` missing from catalog")),
151:         }
152:     }
153: 
154:     for (enum_name, def) in &catalog.enums {
155:         if !catalog.property_ids.contains_key(&def.property) {
156:             errors.push(format!(
157:                 "enum `{enum_name}` references unknown property `{}`",
158:                 def.property
159:             ));
160:         }
161:         if def.values.is_empty() {
162:             errors.push(format!("enum `{enum_name}` has no values"));
163:         }
164:     }
165: 
166:     errors
167: }

173: fn java_dir(repo_root: &Path) -> PathBuf {
174:     repo_root.join("lib/java/pathland-demo/src/main/java/pathland")
175: }
176: 
177: fn write_java(path: &Path, content: &str) {
178:     std::fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap()).expect("create java dir");
179:     std::fs::write(path, content).expect("write java file");
180: }

182: fn header(file: &str) -> String {
183:     format!(
184:         "// GENERATED by pathland-codegen — DO NOT EDIT.\n// Source of truth: lib/ui/components.yaml ({file})\n"
185:     )
186: }
187: 
188: /// Java constant name for a component id (e.g. `Constants.HSTACK`).
189: fn component_const(name: &str) -> String {
190:     format!("Constants.{}", name.to_ascii_uppercase())
191: }
192: 
193: /// Java constant name for a property id (e.g. `Constants.PROP_ALIGNMENT`).
194: fn property_const(name: &str) -> String {
195:     format!("Constants.PROP_{}", name.to_ascii_uppercase())
196: }
197: 
198: /// Escape a DSL name into a valid Java method identifier (append `_` for
199: /// reserved keywords, e.g. `switch` -> `switch_`).
200: fn java_ident(name: &str) -> String {
201:     const JAVA_KEYWORDS: &[&str] = &[
202:         "abstract", "assert", "boolean", "break", "byte", "case", "catch", "char", "class",
203:         "const", "continue", "default", "do", "double", "else", "enum", "extends", "final",
204:         "finally", "float", "for", "goto", "if", "implements", "import", "instanceof", "int",
205:         "interface", "long", "native", "new", "package", "private", "protected", "public",
206:         "return", "short", "static", "strictfp", "super", "switch", "synchronized", "this",
207:         "throw", "throws", "transient", "try", "void", "volatile", "while", "true", "false",
208:         "null",
209:     ];
210:     if JAVA_KEYWORDS.contains(&name) {
211:         format!("{name}_")
212:     } else {
213:         name.to_string()
214:     }
215: }

221: fn emit_constants(catalog: &Catalog, repo_root: &Path) {
222:     let mut out = String::new();
223:     out.push_str(&header("Constants"));
224:     out.push_str("package pathland;\n\n");
225:     out.push_str("/** Protocol ids and size sentinels (mirrors pathland_opcode::constants). */\n");
226:     out.push_str("public final class Constants {\n");
227:     out.push_str("    private Constants() {}\n\n");
228: 
229:     out.push_str("    // --- size sentinels (WIDTH / HEIGHT) ---\n");
230:     out.push_str(&format!("    public static final float FILL = {}f;\n", size::FILL));
231:     out.push_str(&format!(
232:         "    public static final float HUG_CONTENT = {}f;\n",
233:         size::HUG_CONTENT
234:     ));
235: 
236:     out.push_str("\n    // --- component ids ---\n");
237:     for (name, id) in &catalog.component_ids {
238:         out.push_str(&format!(
239:             "    public static final int {} = 0x{:04X};\n",
240:             name.to_ascii_uppercase(),
241:             id
242:         ));
243:     }
244: 
245:     out.push_str("\n    // --- property ids ---\n");
246:     for (name, id) in &catalog.property_ids {
247:         out.push_str(&format!(
248:             "    public static final int PROP_{} = 0x{:04X};\n",
249:             name.to_ascii_uppercase(),
250:             id
251:         ));
252:     }
253: 
254:     out.push_str("}\n");
255:     write_java(&java_dir(repo_root).join("Constants.java"), &out);
256: }

258: fn emit_enum(name: &str, def: &EnumDef, catalog: &Catalog, repo_root: &Path) {
259:     let prop_id = catalog.property_ids.get(&def.property).copied().unwrap_or(0);
260:     let mut out = String::new();
261:     out.push_str(&header(&format!("enum `{name}`")));
262:     out.push_str("package pathland;\n\n");
263:     out.push_str(&format!(
264:         "/** Typed `{name}` values. Wire value is the protocol ENUM value; property `{}` = 0x{:04X}. */\n",
265:         def.property, prop_id
266:     ));
267:     out.push_str(&format!("public enum {name} {{\n"));
268:     let value_count = def.values.len();
269:     for (i, (value_name, value)) in def.values.iter().enumerate() {
270:         let sep = if i + 1 == value_count { ";" } else { "," };
271:         out.push_str(&format!(
272:             "    {}({}){sep}\n",
273:             value_name.to_ascii_uppercase(),
274:             value
275:         ));
276:     }
277:     out.push_str("\n    public final int wire;\n");
278:     out.push_str(&format!(
279:         "    public final int property = {};\n",
280:         property_const(&def.property)
281:     ));
282:     out.push_str("\n    public int wire() { return wire; }\n");
283:     out.push_str(&format!(
284:         "\n    {name}(int wire) {{ this.wire = wire; }}\n"
285:     ));
286:     out.push_str("}\n");
287:     write_java(&java_dir(repo_root).join(format!("{name}.java")), &out);
288: }

290: fn emit_component_node(repo_root: &Path) {
291:     let mut out = String::new();
292:     out.push_str(&header("ComponentNode"));
293:     out.push_str("package pathland;\n\n");
294:     out.push_str("import java.util.ArrayList;\n");
295:     out.push_str("import java.util.List;\n\n");
296:     out.push_str("/** A component node (mirrors a DSL component). Constructor props are set on build. */\n");
297:     out.push_str("public final class ComponentNode implements View {\n");
298:     out.push_str("    private final int componentId;\n");
299:     out.push_str("    private final String text;\n");
300:     out.push_str("    private final List<View> children = new ArrayList<>();\n");
301:     out.push_str("    private final java.util.Map<Integer, Float> constructorProps = new java.util.LinkedHashMap<>();\n\n");
302:     out.push_str("    public ComponentNode(int componentId, String text, List<View> children) {\n");
303:     out.push_str("        this.componentId = componentId;\n");
304:     out.push_str("        this.text = text;\n");
305:     out.push_str("        this.children.addAll(children);\n");
306:     out.push_str("    }\n\n");
307:     out.push_str("    public ComponentNode setConstructorProp(int property, float value) {\n");
308:     out.push_str("        constructorProps.put(property, value);\n");
309:     out.push_str("        return this;\n");
310:     out.push_str("    }\n\n");
311:     out.push_str("    @Override\n");
312:     out.push_str("    public Node build() {\n");
313:     out.push_str("        Node node = new Node(0, componentId);\n");
314:     out.push_str("        if (text != null) node.string = text;\n");
315:     out.push_str("        node.properties.putAll(constructorProps);\n");
316:     out.push_str("        for (View child : children) node.children.add(child.build());\n");
317:     out.push_str("        return node;\n");
318:     out.push_str("    }\n");
319:     out.push_str("}\n");
320:     write_java(&java_dir(repo_root).join("ComponentNode.java"), &out);
321: }

323: fn emit_view(catalog: &Catalog, repo_root: &Path) {
324:     let mut out = String::new();
325:     out.push_str(&header("View"));
326:     out.push_str("package pathland;\n\n");
327:     out.push_str("/**\n");
328:     out.push_str(" * A composable view. Implementations build a {@link Node} subtree.\n");
329:     out.push_str(" *\n");
330:     out.push_str(" * Global modifiers are chainable on any view. The compound `frame` modifier\n");
331:     out.push_str(" * sizes a view (FILL/HUG_CONTENT sentinels) and optionally aligns it.\n");
332:     out.push_str(" */\n");
333:     out.push_str("public interface View {\n");
334:     out.push_str("    Node build();\n\n");
335: 
336:     for m in &catalog.modifiers {
337:         // Skip string-valued properties (e.g. font_family): the Java bridge
338:         // currently round-trips float properties only. They remain in the
339:         // catalog for future languages.
340:         if m.ty == "string" {
341:             continue;
342:         }
343:         let method = m.property.clone();
344:         let (jt, arg) = match m.ty.as_str() {
345:             "bool" => ("boolean".to_string(), "value".to_string()),
346:             "enum" => (
347:                 m.r#enum.as_deref().unwrap_or("int").to_string(),
348:                 "value".to_string(),
349:             ),
350:             "color" => ("int".to_string(), "rgba".to_string()),
351:             _ => ("float".to_string(), "value".to_string()),
352:         };
353:         let value_expr = match m.ty.as_str() {
354:             "color" => format!("Float.intBitsToFloat({arg})"),
355:             "bool" => format!("{arg} ? 1f : 0f"),
356:             "enum" => format!("{arg}.wire"),
357:             _ => arg.to_string(),
358:         };
359:         out.push_str(&format!(
360:             "    default View {method}({jt} {arg}) {{\n"
361:         ));
362:         out.push_str(&format!(
363:             "        return new Modified(this, {}, {value_expr});\n",
364:             property_const(&m.property)
365:         ));
366:         out.push_str("    }\n\n");
367:     }
368: 
369:     out.push_str("    /**\n");
370:     out.push_str("     * Attach a tap gesture (SwiftUI {@code onTapGesture}) to any view.\n");
371:     out.push_str("     * {@code action} runs when a tap is recognized from the view's raw\n");
372:     out.push_str("     * pointer events (down then up on the same target).\n");
373:     out.push_str("     */\n");
374:     out.push_str("    default View onTapGesture(Runnable action) {\n");
375:     out.push_str("        return new TapGesture(this, action);\n");
376:     out.push_str("    }\n\n");
377: 
378:     out.push_str("    /**\n");
379:     out.push_str("     * Compound sizing modifier. Pass {@link Constants#FILL} / {@link Constants#HUG_CONTENT}\n");
380:     out.push_str("     * for a fixed axis, or {@code Float.NaN} to leave it to the native renderer.\n");
381:     out.push_str("     *\n");
382:     out.push_str("     * @param width     width hint (FILL / HUG_CONTENT / NaN for unset)\n");
383:     out.push_str("     * @param height    height hint (FILL / HUG_CONTENT / NaN for unset)\n");
384:     out.push_str("     * @param alignment cross-axis alignment, or null for unset\n");
385:     out.push_str("     */\n");
386:     out.push_str("    default View frame(float width, float height, Align alignment) {\n");
387:     out.push_str("        java.util.Map<Integer, Float> props = new java.util.LinkedHashMap<>();\n");
388:     out.push_str("        if (!Float.isNaN(width)) props.put(Constants.PROP_WIDTH, width);\n");
389:     out.push_str("        if (!Float.isNaN(height)) props.put(Constants.PROP_HEIGHT, height);\n");
390:     out.push_str("        if (alignment != null) props.put(Constants.PROP_ALIGNMENT, (float) alignment.wire);\n");
391:     out.push_str("        return new Modified(this, props);\n");
392:     out.push_str("    }\n");
393:     out.push_str("}\n");
394:     write_java(&java_dir(repo_root).join("View.java"), &out);
395: }

397: fn emit_dsl(catalog: &Catalog, repo_root: &Path) {
398:     let mut out = String::new();
399:     out.push_str(&header("DSL"));
400:     out.push_str("package pathland;\n\n");
401:     out.push_str("import java.util.Arrays;\n");
402:     out.push_str("import java.util.List;\n\n");
403:     out.push_str("/**\n");
404:     out.push_str(" * Static DSL entry points. Component CONSTRUCTOR properties are passed as\n");
405:     out.push_str(" * constructor args (never chainable); global modifiers chain on any view.\n");
406:     out.push_str(" */\n");
407:     out.push_str("public final class DSL {\n");
408:     out.push_str("    private DSL() {}\n\n");
409: 
410:     for (name, comp) in &catalog.components {
411:         let comp_const = component_const(name);
412:         let method = java_ident(name);
413:         let has_text = comp.text_content;
414:         let has_children = comp.children;
415: 
416:         // 1) Default factory.
417:         let default_doc = if has_text {
418:             format!("Create a {} with the given text content.", comp.label)
419:         } else if has_children {
420:             format!("Create a {} with the given children.", comp.label)
421:         } else {
422:             format!("Create a {}.", comp.label)
423:         };
424:         out.push_str(&format!("    /** {default_doc} */\n"));
425:         if has_text {
426:             out.push_str(&format!(
427:                 "    public static View {method}(String content) {{\n"
428:             ));
429:             out.push_str(&format!(
430:                 "        return new ComponentNode({comp_const}, content, java.util.Collections.emptyList());\n"
431:             ));
432:         } else if has_children {
433:             out.push_str(&format!("    public static View {method}(View... children) {{\n"));
434:             out.push_str(&format!(
435:                 "        return new ComponentNode({comp_const}, null, Arrays.asList(children));\n"
436:             ));
437:         } else {
438:             out.push_str(&format!("    public static View {method}() {{\n"));
439:             out.push_str(&format!(
440:                 "        return new ComponentNode({comp_const}, null, java.util.Collections.emptyList());\n"
441:             ));
442:         }
443:         out.push_str("    }\n\n");
444: 
445:         // 2) Constructor-properties overload (only if the component has any).
446:         if !comp.constructor_props.is_empty() {
447:             let mut params = Vec::new();
448:             let mut setter_calls = Vec::new();
449:             for prop in &comp.constructor_props {
450:                 let jt = match prop.ty.as_str() {
451:                     "enum" => prop.r#enum.as_deref().unwrap_or("int").to_string(),
452:                     "u32" => "int".to_string(),
453:                     "bool" => "boolean".to_string(),
454:                     _ => "float".to_string(),
455:                 };
456:                 let pname = short_name(&prop.property);
457:                 params.push(format!("{jt} {pname}"));
458:                 let wire_expr = match prop.ty.as_str() {
459:                     "enum" => format!("{pname}.wire"),
460:                     "bool" => format!("{pname} ? 1f : 0f"),
461:                     "u32" => format!("(float) {pname}"),
462:                     _ => pname.clone(),
463:                 };
464:                 setter_calls.push(format!(
465:                     "        node.setConstructorProp({}, {});\n",
466:                     property_const(&prop.property),
467:                     wire_expr
468:                 ));
469:             }
470:             params.push(if has_text {
471:                 "String content".to_string()
472:             } else if has_children {
473:                 "View... children".to_string()
474:             } else {
475:                 String::new()
476:             });
477:             let params = params
478:                 .into_iter()
479:                 .filter(|p| !p.is_empty())
480:                 .collect::<Vec<_>>()
481:                 .join(", ");
482: 
483:             out.push_str(&format!(
484:                 "    /** Create a {} with constructor properties (structural/layout — never chainable). */\n",
485:                 comp.label
486:             ));
487:             out.push_str(&format!(
488:                 "    public static View {method}({params}) {{\n"
489:             ));
490:             let node_ctor = if has_text {
491:                 format!(
492:                     "new ComponentNode({comp_const}, content, java.util.Collections.emptyList())"
493:                 )
494:             } else if has_children {
495:                 format!("new ComponentNode({comp_const}, null, Arrays.asList(children))")
496:             } else {
497:                 format!("new ComponentNode({comp_const}, null, java.util.Collections.emptyList())")
498:             };
499:             out.push_str(&format!("        ComponentNode node = {node_ctor};\n"));
500:             for call in setter_calls {
501:                 out.push_str(&call);
502:             }
503:             out.push_str("        return node;\n");
504:             out.push_str("    }\n\n");
505:         }
506:     }
507: 
508:     out.push_str("}\n");
509:     write_java(&java_dir(repo_root).join("DSL.java"), &out);
510: }
511: 
512: fn short_name(prop: &str) -> String {
513:     prop.replace('_', "")
514: }

516: fn emit_modified(repo_root: &Path) {
517:     let mut out = String::new();
518:     out.push_str(&header("Modified"));
519:     out.push_str("package pathland;\n\n");
520:     out.push_str("/**\n");
521:     out.push_str(" * A view wrapped by one or more property modifiers (innermost-first).\n");
522:     out.push_str(" * Simple modifiers use the single-property constructor; the compound\n");
523:     out.push_str(" * `frame` modifier uses the map constructor for width/height/alignment.\n");
524:     out.push_str(" */\n");
525:     out.push_str("final class Modified implements View {\n");
526:     out.push_str("    private final View inner;\n");
527:     out.push_str("    private final java.util.Map<Integer, Float> props;\n\n");
528:     out.push_str("    Modified(View inner, int propertyId, float value) {\n");
529:     out.push_str("        this.inner = inner;\n");
530:     out.push_str("        this.props = new java.util.LinkedHashMap<>();\n");
531:     out.push_str("        this.props.put(propertyId, value);\n");
532:     out.push_str("    }\n\n");
533:     out.push_str("    Modified(View inner, java.util.Map<Integer, Float> props) {\n");
534:     out.push_str("        this.inner = inner;\n");
535:     out.push_str("        this.props = props;\n");
536:     out.push_str("    }\n\n");
537:     out.push_str("    @Override\n");
538:     out.push_str("    public Node build() {\n");
539:     out.push_str("        Node node = inner.build();\n");
540:     out.push_str("        node.properties.putAll(props);\n");
541:     out.push_str("        return node;\n");
542:     out.push_str("    }\n");
543:     out.push_str("}\n");
544:     write_java(&java_dir(repo_root).join("Modified.java"), &out);
545: }

551: fn main() {
552:     let repo_root = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
553:         .ancestors()
554:         .nth(4)
555:         .expect("resolve repo root");
556: 
557:     let catalog_path = repo_root.join("lib/ui/components.yaml");
558:     let catalog_text = std::fs::read_to_string(&catalog_path)
559:         .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("read {}: {e}", catalog_path.display()));
560:     let catalog: Catalog =
561:         serde_yaml::from_str(&catalog_text).expect("parse lib/ui/components.yaml");
562: 
563:     let errors = assert_ids(&catalog);
564:     if !errors.is_empty() {
565:         eprintln!("pathland-codegen: catalog/constants mismatch:");
566:         for e in &errors {
567:             eprintln!("  - {e}");
568:         }
569:         std::process::exit(1);
570:     }

2: //! render-tree decode.

4: use pathland_host::RenderTree;

9: #[test]
10: fn flat_builder_emit_then_render_tree() {
11:     let mut host = NativeHost::new();
12: 
13:     // Build: vstack(1) + [ text(2, "Hello"), button(3) ]
14:     host.create_node(1, pathland_view::Component::VStack);
15:     host.create_node(2, pathland_view::Component::Text { text: "".into() });
16:     host.create_node(3, pathland_view::Component::Button { label: "".into() });
17:     host.set_text(2, "Hello");
18:     host.set_property_f32(1, property_id::SPACING, 8.0);
19:     host.insert_child(1, 2, u32::MAX);
20:     host.insert_child(1, 3, u32::MAX);
21: 
22:     assert!(host.emit(), "a frame must be written");
23: 
24:     // The header shows a completed frame (frameCount incremented).
25:     {
26:         let mem = host.ring_buffer();
27:         let header = SharedHeader::new(mem);
28:         assert!(header.frame_count() >= 1);
29:     }
30: 
31:     // Drain the ring and decode the emitted frame into a RenderTree.
32:     let mut render = RenderTree::default();
33:     let mut ring = host.take_ring();
34:     if let Some(batch) = ring.next_frame().unwrap() {
35:         render.apply_frame(batch.frame());
36:     }
37:     assert_eq!(render.nodes.len(), 3);
38:     assert_eq!(render.node(2).unwrap().text.as_deref(), Some("Hello"));
39:     let root = render.node(1).unwrap();
40:     assert_eq!(root.component_type, pathland_opcode::component_type::VSTACK);
41:     assert_eq!(root.children, vec![2, 3]);

1: //! Protocol constants: categories, commands, component types, value types, flags.
2: //!
3: //! These constants are part of the wire protocol (see `spec/OPCODE.md`) and MUST
4: //! NOT be renumbered once released.
5: 
6: /// Opcode categories (`Category` field, u8).
7: pub mod category {
8:     /// Tree mutations (guest → host): node create/delete/insert/remove/move.
9:     pub const TREE: u8 = 0x01;
10:     /// Properties and design tokens (guest → host): the constraint properties
11:     /// (spacing, padding, alignment, …) that native renderers use to lay out
12:     /// native elements. The engine does NOT emit rects.
13:     pub const STYLE: u8 = 0x02;
14:     /// Raw input events (host → guest): pointer down/move/up, key down/up.
15:     pub const EVENT: u8 = 0x03;
16:     /// Control (both directions): reset, environment, custom data.
17:     pub const META: u8 = 0x04;
18: }
19: 
20: /// Commands within the `TREE` category.
21: pub mod tree {
22:     /// `A=nodeId, B=componentType (u16, low)`
23:     pub const CREATE_NODE: u8 = 0x01;
24:     /// `A=nodeId`
25:     pub const DELETE_NODE: u8 = 0x02;
26:     /// `A=parentId, B=childId, C=index` (Flags `INSERT_APPEND` = append)
27:     pub const INSERT_CHILD: u8 = 0x03;
28:     /// `A=parentId, B=childId`
29:     pub const REMOVE_CHILD: u8 = 0x04;
30:     /// `A=parentId, B=childId, C=newIndex` (Flags `INSERT_APPEND` = append)
31:     pub const MOVE_CHILD: u8 = 0x05;
32: }
33: 
34: /// Commands within the `STYLE` category.
35: pub mod style {
36:     /// `A=nodeId, B=(valueType << 16) | propertyId, C=value`
37:     pub const SET_PROPERTY: u8 = 0x01;
38:     /// `A=arenaRef (path), B=valueType (u8), C=value`
39:     pub const SET_DESIGN_TOKEN: u8 = 0x02;
40:     /// `A=nodeId, B=arenaRef (utf8)`
41:     pub const SET_TEXT: u8 = 0x03;
42: }
43: 
44: /// Commands within the `EVENT` category.
45: ///
46: /// Events are **raw inputs** (host → guest), each carrying a host-resolved
47: /// `targetId`. High-level interpretations (tap, drag, long-press) are built by
48: /// the guest/app from these raw inputs and are NOT part of the protocol.
49: pub mod event {
50:     /// `A=targetId, B=x (f32), C=y (f32)` (Flags `POINTER_SECONDARY`)
51:     pub const POINTER_DOWN: u8 = 0x01;
52:     /// `A=targetId, B=x (f32), C=y (f32)` (Flags `HOVER_ENTER` / `HOVER_LEAVE`)
53:     pub const POINTER_MOVE: u8 = 0x02;
54:     /// `A=targetId, B=x (f32), C=y (f32)` (Flags `POINTER_SECONDARY`)
55:     pub const POINTER_UP: u8 = 0x03;
56:     /// `A=targetId, B=keyCode (u16, low), C=modifiers (u8, low)` (Flags `KEY_REPEAT`)
57:     pub const KEY_DOWN: u8 = 0x04;
58:     /// `A=targetId, B=keyCode (u16, low), C=modifiers (u8, low)`
59:     pub const KEY_UP: u8 = 0x05;
60: }
61: 
62: /// Commands within the `META` category.
63: pub mod meta {
64:     /// Host must clear all rendered output.
65:     pub const RESET: u8 = 0x01;
66:     /// `A=viewportWidth (f32), B=viewportHeight (f32)` (host → guest)
67:     pub const ENVIRONMENT: u8 = 0x02;
68: }
69: 
70: /// Flag bits used across categories.
71: pub mod flag {
72:     /// `INSERT_CHILD` / `MOVE_CHILD`: append (index = append).
73:     pub const INSERT_APPEND: u16 = 0x0001;
74:     /// `POINTER_DOWN` / `POINTER_UP`: secondary button (bit 0).
75:     pub const POINTER_SECONDARY: u16 = 0x0001;
76:     /// `POINTER_MOVE`: pointer is entering/hovering (bit 0).
77:     pub const HOVER_ENTER: u16 = 0x0001;
78:     /// `POINTER_MOVE`: pointer is leaving (bit 1).
79:     pub const HOVER_LEAVE: u16 = 0x0002;
80:     /// `KEY_DOWN`: key repeat (bit 1).
81:     pub const KEY_REPEAT: u16 = 0x0002;
82: }
83: 
84: /// Bits for the `EVENT_LISTENERS` semantic property (a u32 bitmask).
85: ///
86: /// Each bit requests that a renderer attach native input recognition for the
87: /// matching raw-input event and report it for that node — so any element (not
88: /// just a button) can emit raw events. Bits are independent of the `EVENT`
89: /// command ids; more event kinds can be added later.
90: pub mod listener {
91:     /// `POINTER_DOWN` events (bit 0).
92:     pub const POINTER_DOWN: u32 = 1 << 0;
93:     /// `POINTER_MOVE` events (bit 1).
94:     pub const POINTER_MOVE: u32 = 1 << 1;
95:     /// `POINTER_UP` events (bit 2).
96:     pub const POINTER_UP: u32 = 1 << 2;
97:     /// `KEY_DOWN` events (bit 3).
98:     pub const KEY_DOWN: u32 = 1 << 3;
99:     /// `KEY_UP` events (bit 4).
100:     pub const KEY_UP: u32 = 1 << 4;
101: 
102:     /// All pointer events (down + move + up).
103:     pub const POINTER: u32 = POINTER_DOWN | POINTER_MOVE | POINTER_UP;
104: }
105: 
106: /// Value types for `STYLE` properties (u8, encoded in the high byte of `B`).
107: pub mod value_type {
108:     pub const U8: u8 = 0x01;
109:     pub const U32: u8 = 0x02;
110:     pub const I32: u8 = 0x03;
111:     pub const F32: u8 = 0x04;
112:     pub const STRING: u8 = 0x05;
113:     pub const ENUM: u8 = 0x06;
114:     pub const COLOR: u8 = 0x07;
115:     pub const DESIGN_TOKEN: u8 = 0x08;
116: }
117: 
118: /// Component types (u16, encoded in the low half of `A` of `TREE::CREATE_NODE`).
119: ///
120: /// IDs are specified in `spec/OPCODE.md` (carried forward from the historical protocol).
121: pub mod component_type {
122:     pub const HSTACK: u16 = 0x0001;
123:     pub const VSTACK: u16 = 0x0002;
124:     pub const TEXT: u16 = 0x0003;
125:     pub const BUTTON: u16 = 0x0004;
126:     pub const IMAGE: u16 = 0x0005;
127:     pub const SWITCH: u16 = 0x0006;
128:     pub const TEXT_FIELD: u16 = 0x0007;
129:     pub const SPACER: u16 = 0x0008;
130:     pub const SCROLLVIEW: u16 = 0x0009;
131:     pub const LIST: u16 = 0x000A;
132:     pub const GRID: u16 = 0x000B;
133:     pub const COMMENT: u16 = 0x000C;
134: }
135: 
136: /// Property IDs (u16, encoded in the low half of `B` of `STYLE::SET_PROPERTY`).
137: ///
138: /// IDs are specified in `spec/OPCODE.md` (carried forward from the historical protocol).
139: pub mod property_id {
140:     // Stack
141:     pub const SPACING: u16 = 0x0001;
142:     pub const ALIGNMENT: u16 = 0x0002;
143:     // 0x0003 reserved (formerly JUSTIFICATION; main-axis distribution is
144:     // expressed via a spacer element instead).
145:     // 0x0004 reserved (formerly PADDING; now a styling modifier at 0x1011).
146:     pub const CONTENT_MARGINS: u16 = 0x0005;
147:     // Text
148:     pub const TEXT: u16 = 0x000A;
149:     pub const LINE_LIMIT: u16 = 0x000B;
150:     pub const TEXT_ALIGNMENT: u16 = 0x000C;
151:     pub const TRUNCATION_MODE: u16 = 0x000D;
152:     // Style (0x1000 range)
153:     pub const BACKGROUND_COLOR: u16 = 0x1001;
154:     pub const BORDER_WIDTH: u16 = 0x1003;
155:     pub const BORDER_COLOR: u16 = 0x1004;
156:     pub const BORDER_RADIUS: u16 = 0x1005;
157:     pub const PADDING_STYLE: u16 = 0x1006;
158:     pub const FONT_SIZE: u16 = 0x1007;
159:     pub const FONT_WEIGHT: u16 = 0x1008;
160:     pub const FONT_FAMILY: u16 = 0x1009;
161:     pub const COLOR: u16 = 0x100A;
162:     pub const WIDTH: u16 = 0x100B;
163:     pub const HEIGHT: u16 = 0x100C;
164:     pub const OPACITY: u16 = 0x100D;
165:     pub const VISIBLE: u16 = 0x100E;
166:     pub const Z_INDEX: u16 = 0x100F;
167:     pub const CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS: u16 = 0x1010;
168:     pub const PADDING: u16 = 0x1011;

173:     // Semantic (0x2000 range)

175:     pub const STATE: u16 = 0x2002;

178:     /// `EVENT_LISTENERS` — a u32 bitmask (see [`crate::listener`]) declaring

6: //! - **Shared memory** (desktop/native): the ring buffer + arena in

8: //!   the local transport — no duplication.

85: ## Engine example
86: 
87: The engine emits declarative structure (no rects). A signal changes a property;
88: the next `emit` writes only the delta opcodes.
89: 
90: ```rust
91: use pathland_engine::Engine;
92: use pathland_opcode::{init_memory, Guest, MemoryLayout};
93: use pathland_view::{assign_ids, text, vstack, View, ViewExt};
94: 
95: let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
96: let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
97: init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
98: 
99: let mut guest = Guest::new(&mut mem, &layout);
100: let mut engine = Engine::new();
101: 
102: let mut root = vstack![text("Hello")]
103:     .spacing(4.0)
104:     .padding(8.0)
105:     .build();
106: assign_ids(&mut root, &mut 1);
107: 
108: guest.begin_frame();
109: engine.emit(&root, &mut guest).unwrap(); // full structure
110: guest.end_frame();
111: 
112: root.properties.insert(pathland_opcode::property_id::SPACING, 12.0f32.to_bits());
113: 
114: guest.begin_frame();
115: engine.emit(&root, &mut guest).unwrap(); // exactly one SET_PROPERTY
116: guest.end_frame();
117: ```
118: 
119: Emission in the steady state allocates nothing; only changed nodes produce
120: opcodes, so an unchanged tree emits zero opcodes. Native renderers map the
121: structure onto their native elements (GTK4 widgets, DOM elements).

101: | `pathland-gtk` | GTK4 renderer (rlib + cdylib): opcode frames → native GTK widgets, incrementally |

88: ### Native C-ABI shim (`pathland-view-native`)
89: 
90: The **desktop/cross-language zero-copy path**: a native `cdylib` exposing the
91: flat world (same semantics as `wit/pathland.wit`) as `pathland_native_*` C
92: functions, with a **shared-memory ring** the host driver reads in place. Any
93: language that links the dylib (Swift/Java/C# via FFI) calls the flat surface —
94: no per-component wrappers — and consumes opcodes zero-copy. The Java demo
95: (`lib/java/pathland-demo`) demonstrates this with a SwiftUI-like Java DSL over
96: JNA. wasmtime/WIT remain only for remote/browser hosts.
97: 
98: ### GTK4 Renderer (`pathland-render-gtk`)
99: 
100: The desktop renderer: a single crate that owns **all** GTK/glib/pango usage and
101: maps opcode frames **incrementally** onto native GTK widgets (a retained
102: `id → gtk::Widget` map). Both the Rust demo and the Java demo render through
103: it — the demos **never call GTK or Swing directly**:
104: 
105: - Rust demo links `pathland-render-gtk` as an `rlib` and calls `GtkRenderer::run(...)`
106:   with a wake closure.
107: - Java demo loads `pathland-render-gtk` as a `cdylib` via JNA and calls
108:   `pathland_gtk_run(host, on_event)`; native inputs round-trip as `EVENT`
109:   opcodes through the shared ring. The renderer **writes** the events and
110:   **wakes** the host (no payload); the host drains the event ring itself via
111:   `pathland_native_drain_events` (Rust: `NativeHost::drain_events` /
112:   `RingTransport::drain_events`). Events are never delivered through a
113:   side-channel callback — they flow through the opcode engine.
114: 
115: The renderer maps native inputs onto the raw `Event` surface via GTK4
116: controllers (`Button::clicked` → pointer up, `EventControllerMotion` →
117: pointer move/enter/leave), emitting events through the same `Pump::send_input`
118: path.
119: 
120: `pathland-render-gtk::run` passes an explicit empty argv to GTK (the process command
121: line belongs to the embedding host — e.g. the JVM's `-cp`/`-D` flags — and must
122: not be parsed as GTK options).
123: 
124: ### Catalog-Driven DSL (`lib/ui/components.yaml` + `pathland-codegen`)
125: 
126: The **single source of truth** for the DSL surface: components, per-component
127: constructor props, global modifiers, enums, and ids live in one YAML file. The
128: `pathland-codegen` generator parses it, **asserts every id against
129: `pathland_opcode::constants`** (a hard build error on mismatch — the consistency
130: safety net), and emits the checked-in Java DSL (typed enums, `View`/`DSL`/
131: `ComponentNode`/`Modified`, overloaded factories). Rules (NON-NEGOTIABLE):
132: 
133: - Component **constructor props** (structural/layout) are constructor args, never chainable.
134: - Global **modifiers** (appearance/decoration) are chainable on any view.
135: - `spacing` is a constructor property; `padding` is a modifier (always).
136: - No standalone width/height — use the compound `frame(width, height, alignment)` modifier.
137: - Typed enums (Align/TextAlign/Truncation/FontWeight), not raw ints.
138:

1: //! Batch wire format: encode/decode opcodes + arena delta into network batches.
2: 
3: use alloc::vec::Vec;
4: use pathland_core::{Frame, Opcode};
5: 
6: use crate::{BATCH_MAGIC, BATCH_VERSION};
7: 
8: /// Fixed header byte length: magic(4) + version(2) + flags(2) + frameCount(4) + opcodeCount(4).
9: pub const BATCH_HEADER: usize = 16;
10: 
11: /// Errors produced while decoding a network batch.
12: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
13: pub enum BatchError {
14:     /// The batch is shorter than the fixed header.
15:     Truncated,
16:     /// The batch magic does not match `BATCH_MAGIC`.
17:     BadMagic,
18:     /// The batch version is not supported.
19:     BadVersion,
20:     /// The opcode payload is truncated (opcodeCount × 16 exceeds the buffer).
21:     BadOpcodeCount,
22:     /// The arena delta length exceeds the remaining buffer.
23:     BadArenaLen,
24: }
25: 
26: /// A decoded network batch: opcodes plus a mirrored arena, exposed as a
27: /// `pathland_core::Frame` so consumers (`RenderTree::apply_frame`) work
28: /// exactly as with shared-memory frames.
29: pub struct Batch<'a> {
30:     frame: Frame<'a>,
31:     frame_count: u32,
32:     flags: u16,
33: }
34: 
35: impl<'a> core::fmt::Debug for Batch<'a> {
36:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
37:         f.debug_struct("Batch")
38:             .field("frame_count", &self.frame_count)
39:             .field("flags", &self.flags)
40:             .field("len", &self.len())
41:             .finish()
42:     }
43: }
44: 
45: impl<'a> Batch<'a> {
46:     /// The opcodes carried by this batch, in order.
47:     pub fn opcodes(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = Opcode> + '_ {
48:         self.frame.opcodes()
49:     }
50: 
51:     /// Number of opcodes in the batch.
52:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
53:         self.frame.len()
54:     }
55: 
56:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
57:         self.frame.is_empty()
58:     }
59: 
60:     /// The guest frame count the batch spans.
61:     pub fn frame_count(&self) -> u32 {
62:         self.frame_count
63:     }
64: 
65:     /// Direction flags (see [`crate::direction`]).
66:     pub fn flags(&self) -> u16 {
67:         self.flags
68:     }
69: 
70:     /// View this batch as a `Frame` (the transport seam).
71:     pub fn as_frame(&self) -> &Frame<'a> {
72:         &self.frame
73:     }
74: 
75:     /// Read an arena entry by offset (see `Frame::arena_get`).
76:     pub fn arena_get(&self, offset: u32) -> Result<&'a [u8], pathland_core::ArenaError> {
77:         self.frame.arena_get(offset)
78:     }
79: 
80:     /// Read an arena string by offset.
81:     pub fn arena_str(&self, offset: u32) -> Result<&'a str, pathland_core::ArenaError> {
82:         self.frame.arena_str(offset)
83:     }
84: }
85: 
86: /// Serialize one batch from opcodes + an arena delta (bytes appended since the
87: /// previous batch). Stateless; see [`BatchEncoder`] for cursor tracking.
88: pub fn encode_batch(
89:     frame_count: u32,
90:     flags: u16,
91:     opcodes: &[Opcode],
92:     arena_delta: &[u8],
93: ) -> Vec<u8> {
94:     let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(BATCH_HEADER + opcodes.len() * Opcode::SIZE + arena_delta.len() + 4);
95:     out.extend_from_slice(&BATCH_MAGIC.to_le_bytes());
96:     out.extend_from_slice(&BATCH_VERSION.to_le_bytes());
97:     out.extend_from_slice(&flags.to_le_bytes());
98:     out.extend_from_slice(&frame_count.to_le_bytes());
99:     out.extend_from_slice(&(opcodes.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
100:     for op in opcodes {
101:         out.extend_from_slice(&op.to_bytes());
102:     }
103:     out.extend_from_slice(&(arena_delta.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
104:     out.extend_from_slice(arena_delta);
105:     out
106: }
107: 
108: /// Fields parsed from a batch header + payload regions.
109: struct ParsedBatch<'a> {
110:     flags: u16,
111:     frame_count: u32,
112:     opcodes: &'a [u8],
113:     arena_delta: &'a [u8],
114: }
115: 
116: /// Parse a batch header, returning flags, frame count, opcode bytes and arena delta.
117: fn parse(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<ParsedBatch<'_>, BatchError> {
118:     if bytes.len() < BATCH_HEADER {
119:         return Err(BatchError::Truncated);
120:     }
121:     let magic = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[0..4].try_into().unwrap());
122:     if magic != BATCH_MAGIC {
123:         return Err(BatchError::BadMagic);
124:     }
125:     let version = u16::from_le_bytes(bytes[4..6].try_into().unwrap());
126:     if version != BATCH_VERSION {
127:         return Err(BatchError::BadVersion);
128:     }
129:     let flags = u16::from_le_bytes(bytes[6..8].try_into().unwrap());
130:     let frame_count = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[8..12].try_into().unwrap());
131:     let opcode_count = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[12..16].try_into().unwrap()) as usize;
132: 
133:     let opcodes_bytes = opcode_count
134:         .checked_mul(Opcode::SIZE)
135:         .ok_or(BatchError::BadOpcodeCount)?;
136:     let opcodes_start = BATCH_HEADER;
137:     let opcodes_end = opcodes_start
138:         .checked_add(opcodes_bytes)
139:         .ok_or(BatchError::BadOpcodeCount)?;
140:     if opcodes_end > bytes.len() {
141:         return Err(BatchError::BadOpcodeCount);
142:     }
143:     let arena_len_pos = opcodes_end;
144:     if arena_len_pos + 4 > bytes.len() {
145:         return Err(BatchError::BadArenaLen);
146:     }
147:     let arena_len = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[arena_len_pos..arena_len_pos + 4].try_into().unwrap())
148:         as usize;
149:     let arena_start = arena_len_pos + 4;
150:     let arena_end = arena_start
151:         .checked_add(arena_len)
152:         .ok_or(BatchError::BadArenaLen)?;
153:     if arena_end > bytes.len() {
154:         return Err(BatchError::BadArenaLen);
155:     }
156: 
157:     Ok(ParsedBatch {
158:         flags,
159:         frame_count,
160:         opcodes: &bytes[opcodes_start..opcodes_end],
161:         arena_delta: &bytes[arena_start..arena_end],
162:     })
163: }
164: 
165: /// A streamed network-batch encoder.
166: ///
167: /// Tracks the last arena length so successive batches carry only the bytes
168: /// appended to the bump arena since the previous batch. If the arena is reset
169: /// (shrank — see `META::RESET`), the full used arena is sent and tracking
170: /// restarts.
171: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
172: pub struct BatchEncoder {
173:     last_arena_len: usize,
174: }
175: 
176: impl BatchEncoder {
177:     /// Create a fresh encoder (no arena bytes sent yet).
178:     pub fn new() -> Self {
179:         Self { last_arena_len: 0 }
180:     }
181: 
182:     /// Encode a frame's opcodes plus the arena bytes appended since the last
183:     /// call. `arena_used` is the arena region's used portion (`[0..cursor)`).
184:     ///
185:     /// If the frame contains `META::RESET`, arena tracking restarts (the arena
186:     /// cursor returns to 0) and the full used arena is sent.
187:     pub fn encode(&mut self, frame_count: u32, opcodes: &[Opcode], arena_used: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
