212: /// A streamed network-batch decoder.
213: ///
214: /// Maintains a **mirrored arena**: each batch's arena delta is appended, so
215: /// absolute `arenaRef` offsets resolve exactly as in shared memory. When a
216: /// batch contains `META::RESET`, the mirror is cleared before appending.
217: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
218: pub struct BatchDecoder {
219:     arena: Vec<u8>,
220: }
221: 
222: impl BatchDecoder {
223:     /// Create an empty decoder.
224:     pub fn new() -> Self {
225:         Self { arena: Vec::new() }
226:     }
227: 
228:     /// Decode a batch, appending its arena delta to the mirror.
229:     ///
230:     /// The returned `Batch` borrows `bytes` (opcodes) and this decoder (arena);
231:     /// keep both alive while consuming it.
232:     pub fn decode<'a>(&'a mut self, bytes: &'a [u8]) -> Result<Batch<'a>, BatchError> {
233:         let parsed = parse(bytes)?;
234: 
235:         // A META::RESET in the batch clears the renderer; reset the arena mirror
236:         // to match (offsets restart at 0 after a reset).
237:         let opcode_count = parsed.opcodes.len() / Opcode::SIZE;
238:         let reset = (0..opcode_count).any(|i| {
239:             let op = Opcode::from_bytes(parsed.opcodes[i * Opcode::SIZE..(i + 1) * Opcode::SIZE].try_into().unwrap());
240:             op.category() == pathland_core::category::META
241:                 && op.command() == pathland_core::meta::RESET
242:         });
243:         if reset {
244:             self.arena.clear();
245:         }
246:         self.arena.extend_from_slice(parsed.arena_delta);
247: 
248:         let frame = Frame::from_parts(parsed.opcodes, &self.arena, 0, parsed.opcodes.len());
249:         Ok(Batch {
250:             frame,
251:             frame_count: parsed.frame_count,
252:             flags: parsed.flags,
253:         })
254:     }
255: 
256:     /// The mirrored arena length (diagnostics).
257:     pub fn arena_len(&self) -> usize {
258:         self.arena.len()
259:     }
260: }

content.text:
Done. The refactor is complete on branch `refactor/crate-structure-simplification`.

## Result: 11 crates → 9, each name showing its element

| Element | Crate |
|---|---|
| Retained UI | `pathland-view` (DSL) |
| Opcode engine | `pathland-core` (tree types + diff emitter + opcode/ring/arena), `pathland-core-transport` |
| Renderer | `pathland-render-gtk` (absorbs `pathland-host`) |
| Retained-UI projections | `pathland-view-native`, `pathland-view-guest`, `pathland-view-wit` |
| Tool / demo | `pathland-codegen`, `pathland-render-gtk-demo` |

## Key structural change
`Node`/`Component`/`assign_ids`/`component_type_id`/`value_type_for` moved from `pathland-view` into `pathland-core`, and the diff emitter (`pathland-engine`) merged there too. This breaks the `view ↔ core` dependency cycle so `view` is now a pure DSL over `core`, with `core` depending on nothing.

## Preserved (C ABI / JNA compatibility)
- `[lib] name = "pathland_native"` and `"pathland_gtk"`, so `libpathland_native.dylib` / `libpathland_gtk.dylib` and all `pathland_native_*` / `pathland_gtk_*` symbols are unchanged — verified with `nm` and the Java `DemoHeadless` run (`OK: Java DSL -> Rust engine -> shared ring`).
- `[lib] name = "pathland_guest"` so the WASM output stays `pathland_guest.wasm`.

## Verification
- `cargo test` — all green (incl. 12 new core engine tests + the moved `RenderTree` tests now in `pathland-render-gtk`).
- `cargo component build -p pathland-view-guest` — builds, and `pathland-view-wit` tests pass.
- `cargo build -p pathland-core -p pathland-view --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` — `no_std` preserved.
- `./generate.sh` path verified (regenerated Java, comment-only diff).

## One thing to flag
Rebuilding the WASM guest surfaced a **pre-existing** bug (unrelated to the rename): `take_batch` returned empty bytes for a zero-delta frame, so `pathland-view-wit::reemit_produces_only_deltas` hit `Truncated`. I made a minimal fix — the guest now emits a decodable empty batch when a frame completes with no opcodes (`pathland-view-guest/src/lib.rs:229`). This was masked before by a stale build artifact in `target/`.

Changes are staged but not committed — let me know if you'd like me to commit.
